# A SHORT SUMMARY
## of this BOOK.

Being a **profound** and **deep investigation** into the **threefold life of man** through the **three principles**.

In which is clearly shown that which is **eternal**, and also that which is **mortal**.

And why **God** (who is the **highest good**) has brought all things to light.

<margin>* Or, distinguishes.</margin>
Also why one thing is contrary to another and destroys it; and then what is right (or true) and what is evil or **false**, and how the one separates itself from the other.

In this, the **three principles** are especially established, which are the only origin <term>original: "originall," meaning source</term> or fountain from which all things flow and are generated.

Through this, the multitude of **meanings** and **opinions** about **faith** and **religion** may be known. It also explains the cause of the many **opinions** among **people** <note>original: "Men"</note> concerning the **essence** and **will** of **God**; also what is best for **man** to **do**, so that he may attain the highest and **eternal good**.

And finally, concerning the **end** and **outcome** <note>original: "issue"</note> of **all** things: why all things have appeared in the specific properties and **essence** they possessed, for the comfort of the poor, wounded, and sick **soul** of **man**, and for the **rebuilding** or **edification** of the true

# THE THIRD BOOK
# OF THE AUTHOR.

## A High and Deep Search
->Concerning<-
## *The Threefold Life of Man.*

### Chapter 1.

<margin>1.</margin>
When we consider the beginning of our life and compare it with the eternal life which we have in the promise, we cannot say or find that we are at home in this life. For we see the beginning and the end of the outward <note>The "outward life" refers to our physical, earthly existence in the material world.</note> life, as well as the total decay and final corruption of our bodies. Furthermore, we see or know of no return into this outward life, nor do we have any promise of it from the high and eternal Good <note>original: "Good"—a common term for God as the ultimate source of all goodness.</note>.

2. Seeing then that there is a life in us which is eternal and incorruptible, with which we strive after the highest Good; and a life (from this world) which is finite and corruptible; and also a life in which the source and original cause of life stands, wherein the highest danger of eternal perdition <term>eternal punishment or damnation</term>, misery, and calamity consists; therefore it is necessary that we consider the beginning of life, from where all these things proceed and have their origin.

3. Now, when we consider what life is, we find that it is a burning fire which consumes, and when it has no more fuel to feed upon, it goes out—as may be seen in all fires. For life has its nourishment from the body, and the body from its food; for when the body has no more food, then it is
<meta>catchword: consumed</meta>

<summary>This page introduces the concept of the "threefold life" of humanity, contrasting our temporary physical existence with our eternal spiritual potential. The author uses the metaphor of fire to describe life, noting that it requires constant nourishment and warning of the dangers of eternal spiritual misery.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Boehme, Threefold Life, Eternal Life, mortality, spiritual philosophy, perdition, fire of life</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the three lives in man: the physical (elementary) life, the eternal soul, and the divine life. It explores the concept of the "Mother" as the source of all life and explains the relationship between the Creator and the created world.</meta>

consumed by the fire of the life, so that it fades and perishes, just as a beautiful flower withers when it has no water.

4. Since there is a life in man that is eternal and incorruptible—which is the soul—and since it is also a fire that needs nourishment just as the physical <note>original: "Elementary"</note> life does, we must consider the nature and fuel of that life. We must understand what it is that continually feeds it so that it never goes out throughout eternity.

5. Thirdly, we find in the life of our souls a greater hunger for another, higher, and better life—namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, for the highest Good, which is called the *Divine Life*. The soul is not content with its own food, but it desires the highest and best Good with great longing and gasping, seeking it not just as a pleasant home, but as a food to satisfy its hunger.

6. So we now perceive through our profound and true knowledge that every life desires its own "Mother" (the source from which that life is generated) as food. For example, wood is the mother of fire; the fire desires it, and if it is separated from its mother, it goes out. In the same way, the earth is the mother of all trees and herbs, and they desire it. Water (along with the other elements) is the mother of the earth; without it, the earth would be dead or barren, and neither metals, trees, herbs, nor grass would grow from it.

7. We see especially that the physical <note>original: "Elementary"</note> life consists of a boiling or a kind of seething; when it stops boiling, it goes out. We also know that the constellations kindle the elements, and the stars are the fire of the elements, and the sun kindles the stars, so that there is a boiling and seething among them. But the physical life is finite and corruptible, while the life of the soul is eternal.

8. Now, since it is eternal, it must also come from the Eternal, as the beloved *Moses* wrote very rightly about it: 
> *Then God breathed into man the breath of life, and man became a living soul.* <note>Genesis 2:7</note>

9. Yet we cannot say, even though man exists in a *Threefold Life*, that each life is separate or in a distinct form. Instead, we find that they are within one another, yet each life has its own activity within its own domain—that is, within its "Mother." For just as God the Father is everything (because all comes from Him, He is present everywhere, and He is the fullness of everything), yet the created thing does not contain Him. Also, the thing itself is not God, nor His Spirit, nor the true *Divine Essence*. Therefore, it cannot be said of any physical thing that it *is* God, or that God is more present here than in other places; yet He is truly present. He contains the thing, but the thing does not contain Him. He understands <note>original: "comprehendeth"</note> the thing, and the thing

# Ch: 1. Of the Original Matrix.

<margin>Or: Crude, empty, feeble, or faint.</margin>
10. In the same way, the soul of man is breathed in from God; it dwells in the body and is surrounded by the Spirit of the Stars and Elements. It is not just covered by them like a garment covers the body, but it is infected by the Spirit of the Stars and Elements, just as the plague or other infectious diseases infect the physical <note>original: "Elementary"</note> spirit. This poisons the body so that it decays and dies. Then, the influence <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> of the stars also breaks away from the soul and consumes itself. Consequently, the physical <note>original: "Elementary"</note> Mother <note>the material source of life</note> breaks away, and the Spirit of the Stars no longer has any food and therefore consumes itself; but the soul remains <gloss>crude, empty, or faint</gloss> naked, because it lives by another food.

<margin>Being or substance.</margin>
11. Understand us in this way: although the soul is thus captivated by the Spirit of the Stars and Elements, so that their influence <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> dwells within the soul, the soul still has another food. It lives in another Principle and is another <gloss>being or substance</gloss>.

12. For its essences <note>original: "Essences" refers to the faculties or powers of its substance</note> are not from the *constellations*, but have their beginning and bodily union out of the *Eternal Band*—out of Eternal Nature. This nature belongs to God the Father and existed before the light of His Love, in which He enters into Himself and creates for Himself the second Principle in His Love. From this, He continually generates His Eternal Word and Heart from eternity to eternity. There, the holy name of God continually arises <note>original: "discovereth itself"</note> and maintains its *Divine Nature* as a Spirit within itself in the second Principle; it dwells in nothing else, but purely in itself.

<margin>Or: Sprouting.</margin>
13. For although the band of Eternal Nature is within it, the Divine Spirit is not subjected to that band. Instead, the Spirit kindles that band so that it becomes enlightened and <gloss>sprouting</gloss> with the power of Light in Love, within the life of the Word and Heart of God. In this way, it is a holy dwelling and Paradise for that Spirit which is called God.

14. Likewise, the soul of man comes out of the band of the Eternal Original and stands in it eternally. In its own self, within the second Principle, the soul desires to press into God and to satisfy itself in the power of God. But it cannot enter into the light and power of God with its whole being (with its own essences), just as Eternal Nature cannot press into the Light of God to claim the light as its own power. Instead, the Light shines out of Love in its own Principle within Eternal Nature, so that the Light remains Lord over Eternal Nature. Eternal Nature does not comprehend the Light but rejoices in it,

Instead, it must press into God and His love through another principle <note>original: "Principle" refers to a fundamental realm or state of being</note> within itself.

15. For you must understand here a *new birth in the soul*. It must not only push through the life of the stars and elements but also beyond its own inherent nature <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> of life. It must incline its will toward the Life of God, striving to exist within it. This inclined or created will is received by God, and God dwells in that will. Thus, Divine Life and Light enter the soul, making it a child of God. For the soul then exists in its own nature and life, just as God the Father himself exists in the nature <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> of Eternal Nature.

16. Here we understand that <margin>beyond</margin> without the Divine Light (which is the "second principle"), there is an agonizing nature <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> within Eternal Nature. The bond of life exists within fire; but when that fire is <margin>infected or filled</margin> inspired and captivated by Divine Love, the life within it moves forward into another state <note>original: "source [or property]"</note>. A new principle is opened up for it to live in, and that Life is in God. This is just as God dwells in Himself, yet is truly everything Himself—all things have come from His Nature. However, you must understand that only souls and angelic spirits come from Eternal Nature in this way. Other things come from His <margin>creaturely</margin> created will, which has a beginning—namely, from the external world. Therefore, everything in this outward world is *transitory*. In this, we find the great and terrible *Fall* of our soul through our first parents: the soul entered the spirit of this world (a strange lodging) and forsook the Divine Light, in which it was an angel and a child of God. Therefore, it must leave the spirit of the stars and elements and pass through a *New Birth* back into the Life of God.

17. But because it was impossible for the soul to do this on its own, the Life of God came to us through love and grace in the flesh. He took our human soul back into the Divine Life through the power of the Light, so that we might be able to press into that same life with God through a New Birth. Just as we all departed from the life of God through the soul of *Adam*—for the children of *Adam* inherited everything from their parents' soul, springing from them like branches from a tree—so too has the life of God in Christ regenerated us. This allows us to enter the life of God again through the life of Christ. And so, currently, our soul exists within the bond of the Eternal Source <note>original: "Originall"</note>, yet it is infected by the spirit of this world and held captive by the wrath of that original source in the life

# Ch. 1. Of the Original Matrix or Mother.

...of the eternal fire, namely, in *Eternal Nature*. Therefore, every one of us must personally press with our soul into the Life of Christ, toward God, and into the *New Birth* <note>original: "Regeneration"</note> in the Life and Spirit of Christ. Here, no hypocrisy, outward holiness <note>original: "appearing holinesse"</note>, or any supposedly meritorious works will help at all. The poor soul can *be helped in no other way* except by entering into itself with a new, created will, and with a steadfast, earnest purpose and resolution, into the Life of Christ. Then, it will be received with great <margin>g honor <note>original: "Glory"</note></margin> by God and his children in the second Principle. The noble, precious Treasure—namely, the Light of Eternal Life—will be given to it. This Light illuminates the nature <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> of the soul in the first Principle, where it exists substantially with its inherent powers <note>original: "Essences"</note> forever. It turns anguish into love, and the rising and burning of its own nature into a humble, lovely joy <note>original: "mirth"</note> and gentle delight.

18. Thus, the soul is a joyful dwelling place in the Divine Life. I might compare it to a lit lamp: when the wick of the candle burns, it casts a pleasant light—or shines brightly—and feels no pain in the shining, but only a bright pleasantness. Yet the wick continues burning. You must understand, however, that there is no pain or woe in the burning wick; it is only the cause of the glow of life. No *fire* is comparable to the *Divine* [fire].

19. For the Divine Nature, from which the Divine fire of life burns, is <margin>h inspired and filled <note>original: "inficiret"</note></margin> with the *Love of God*. Thus, the light of God creates another Principle within itself, where the harshness of Nature is not <margin>i perceived <note>original: "felt"</note></margin>, for it is the end [or perfection] of Nature. Therefore, the soul cannot grasp the light of God within its own inherent powers <note>original: "Essences"</note> so as to possess it. The soul is a fire within <margin>k the Eternal Nature <note>original: "that which is Eternal"</note></margin> and does not reach the "end" of Nature on its own. It remains within Nature as a creature created out of the Eternal Nature, which yet cannot be fully grasped. It is a Spirit in a sevenfold form. In the <margin>l origin <note>original: "Originality"</note></margin>, there are not seven forms but only four known forms that uphold the Eternal Bond. Those [four] forms are the nature <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> of Anguish, in which <margin>k the Eternal</margin> exists. Out of those, the *other forms* are completely <margin>l generated <note>original: "Birth"</note></margin>—those in which God and the Kingdom of Heaven exist. In the [first] four forms, anguish and torment exist if they are left alone; in those, we understand Hell-fire and the Eternal wrath of God to reside. And although we do not know the very origin of God’s Essence, we know the Eternal <margin>l Birth <note>original: "Geniture"</note></margin>, which never had a beginning. Since it had no beginning, it is the same today as it has been from eternity. Therefore, we may well understand what we see and know today in the Light of God.

20. No one should consider us ignorant, because God has given...

# Ch. 1. Of the Original Matrix or Mother.

...us to know his own <margin>m being or substance</margin> essence, which we cannot and must not deny, under penalty of losing the *Divine Light* and our eternal salvation. It is impossible for any man to have this light unless it is given to him out of grace in the love of God. When that is given to a man, then that soul stands in the knowledge of the wonders of God. That soul then speaks not of strange and distant things, but of the things in which it exists and of itself; for it becomes "seeing" in the light of God, so that it *can know itself.*

21. Consider how this can be: the soul's inherent powers <note>original: "essences"</note> exist in the *original* within the *first principle* <note>In Boehme's theosophy, the "First Principle" is the dark, fiery foundation of nature and the wrath of God</note>, and the *Divine Light* shines within itself and creates the *second principle* <note>The "Second Principle" is the world of light, love, and divine grace</note>. Thus, there are two of them. The soul sees into the high knowledge of the light of the second principle which shines within it. Why then should it not speak of its native country where it lives? And how will you, mad world—existing in the *third principle* <note>The "Third Principle" is the physical, material world governed by the stars and elements</note> in the spirit [or wisdom] of the stars and elements—forbid it from doing so? For you are blind toward God and lie captured in the eternal wrath, within the nature <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> of the *original*.

22. Since this is so, we will set down the *basis* <note>original: "ground"</note> of the *eternal bond* as a mirror for anyone who desires to see. However, it is true that he cannot learn it from *us* unless he himself enters into the *new birth into the life of Christ*, so that the Divine Light itself may shine in him. Otherwise, <margin>n what is written here will be like a history book without any understanding of the mysterious wisdom hidden beneath it</margin> we are only like a history book to him and will not be understood.

23. When we speak of the source [or origin] of the fire and its ignition (meaning the fire of life), we know for certain that in its origin, before the fire is lit, it consists only of two forms and has but one Mother. This Mother is <margin>o astringent or attractive</margin> harsh and draws things to herself; yet there is nothing within her but a "willing" of the *eternal* Father in the eternal nature, which he has appointed within himself to reveal and declare his wonders.

24. Now, that will is eternal and is not stirred up by anything except itself. If it did not exist, everything would be nothing—neither darkness nor light. Therefore, since something does exist, it must be the eternal will. That will is astringent and <margin>p desires to create wonders</margin> desirous of the *wonders of the creation*. Because there is a desire, the desire attracts things to itself, and what is attracted into the desire fills the will, so that the desire is fulfilled. For the will is as thin [or empty] as <margin>q a vacuum</margin> nothingness; but what is attracted into the will makes it thick [or dense and full], and that is its darkness. The eternal desire exists within that darkness.

But because the Will is an eternal desiring, it attracts to itself eternally. Having nothing else to attract, it attracts itself and impregnates [or fills] itself. Thus, the nothingness becomes a darkness, and the attraction <margin>Is the spur to the beginning of the being of a thing.</margin> creates the sting of the first essences <note>In this context, "essences" refers to the fundamental properties or "powers" that make up a being</note>, so that there is a stirring and an origin of mobility.

26. Now the Will cannot tolerate the attraction and impregnation, for it wishes to be free; yet it cannot be, because it is desiring. Seeing that it cannot be free, it enters into itself along with the attraction and conceives [or takes] within itself *another Will*. This second will is to go out from the darkness into itself. That other conceived Will is the *Eternal Mind*, and it enters into itself like a sudden flash [of lightning] and *dissipates* the darkness. It goes forth into itself and dwells in itself, creating for itself *another* [or second] principle of a different quality <note>original: "source or condition"</note>, for the sting of the stirring remains behind in the darkness.

For the attracting sourness desires the strong *shutting up in death*, while the stinging bitterness is the *opener*; yet bitterness would be nothing in itself without the Will.

29. Now, when the sourness attracts so strongly, it cannot tolerate the stinging—that is, the sourness’s own attraction—but stirs much more. <meta>This page continues the exploration of the "Eternal Nature" and the birth of existence. It details how the internal struggle between the "Will" and the "Desire" creates a state of "anguish" or "mobility," which Boehme identifies as the root of all life and manifestation.</meta>

# Chapter 1. Of the Original Mother <note>original: "Genetrix or Matrix"</note>.

### The Origin of the Spirit or Eternal Nature within the Eternal Will.

<margin>
b Or, sound.
</margin>
31. For the four-fold desire attracts and creates penetration, and the bitterness breaks it apart within the turning wheel [of nature]. This results in a multiplicity of essences <note>original: "Essences"; the fundamental powers or building blocks of being</note>. It is almost like a fury, or to use a metaphor, a confusion of the Eternal Mobility, which is the cause of the essences. The Eternal Will must allow this to exist within itself. Therefore, it conceives or adopts another Will to escape from this wheel, yet it cannot, because this wheel is its own substance. Since it cannot escape, and yet cannot abandon its eternal desire and longing, it holds and attracts itself. Consequently, the essences are continually generated, though without the desiring, they would be nothing. Thus, the whole form exists in this noise and is called *MAR* <note>original: "MAR"; Boehme likely connects this to the Latin *mare* (sea) and the Hebrew *mar* (bitter), representing the turbulent, "salty" source of nature</note>. Because the Will cannot be free, it falls into a great *anguish*—to speak in human terms so that the *reader* may understand its depth.

32. The Will is the act of conceiving, and what is conceived within the Will is its Darkness. The desiring is the Essence, and the opposing will is the wheel of the multiple essences. These are countless, and their number corresponds to the degree of mobility [movement]. These two forms are the Eternal Essences and the Eternal *Band* [or bond] that creates itself and cannot do otherwise.

33. For vast, infinite space desires narrowness and enclosure [or comprehension] so that it may manifest itself. Otherwise, in the wide *stillness*, there would be no manifestation. Therefore, there must be an *attraction* and an enclosure from which the manifestation appears. Because of this, there must also be an opposing Will; a transparent and quiet will is like nothing and generates nothing. But if a Will is to generate, it must be within something where it can take form and create. For "nothing" is simply a *stillness* without any movement, where there is neither darkness nor light, nor life nor death.

<margin>
c Or, senses [perceptions].
</margin>

This world *is* not outside of this place [our world], but exists in another property and in the Eternal Light. Yet there could be no light unless there were a *Mother* [original: *Genetrix* or *Matrix*] to bring it forth.

37. You say, "God has created it." Very well; but why are you blind and why do you not acknowledge it, seeing as you are made in the likeness of God? 38. Since God is the Word that has made all things, He must therefore be *in all things*. For a spirit is not a "made" thing, but something generated within itself, which has the *center* <note>original: "Centre"; in Böhme's philosophy, this is the point of origin where divine energy becomes manifest nature</note> of its birth within itself; otherwise, it would be corruptible. For there is nothing from eternity but the *Word*, and the Word was God; therefore, it must necessarily be its *own Eternal Maker*. It must express itself as a Word out of itself, as if out of its own Maker.

### The Origin of the Spirit or Eternal Nature in the Eternal Will.

31. For the fourfold desire <note>In Böhme’s system, these are the four primary properties of nature: harshness, bitterness, anguish, and fire.</note> attracts and creates penetration, and the bitterness breaks it apart in the turning wheel; thus, a multiplicity of inner qualities <note>original: "Essences"</note> arises. It is like a fury or—to use a metaphor—a confusion of Eternal Motion, which is the cause of all qualities. The Eternal Will must allow this to exist within itself. *Therefore*, it conceives or takes unto itself *another will* to escape from this wheel. Yet it cannot do so, for this motion is its own substance. Since it cannot escape, and yet cannot abandon its eternal desire and longing, it holds and attracts itself. Thus, these qualities are continually generated, and yet (without this desiring) they would be nothing. In this way, the whole form exists in the <margin>b Or, found.</margin>b sound or noise, and is called *M A R* <note>Böhme associates "MAR" with the Latin *mare* (sea) and the root of bitterness, representing the turbulent source of nature.</note>. Thus, the *Father* is *not* in the source [or *quality*] of *Darkness*; for the re-comprehended *Will* (which goes forth out of the *Center* and dispels the *Darkness*) is his *Heart* and dwells in itself. It enlightens the *Father* [or is the radiance and light or luster of the Father]. That *Will* is the *Word of the Eternal Father*, which is generated out of the *Eternal Essences* and is rightly *another Person*. For he dwells in the *Father's Essences* [or *Essential powers*] in himself and is the *Light of the Father*. This *Word* (or *Will*) has created all things—understand, out of the *Essences* of the *Father*—for it [the *Word*] is the *Eternal Omnipotence*. This is because it cannot be comprehended <note>original: comprehended; contained or limited</note> by the *Eternal Essences*; instead, it breaks asunder the *Eternal Essences* and dwells in itself, shining out of the *Essences*. Yet it cannot depart from the *Essences*, any more than the radiance or light departs from a fire.

13. For the will is as subtle <insert>or empty</insert> as if it were *nothing*, and very still and quiet. The desiring attracts all the more vehemently to itself, and so the sting or prickling is greater, and it rages against the attraction. Yet it cannot escape from it, for the desiring generates it, and yet cannot endure it; for it is such an enmity as exists between heat and cold.

53. We also give you this very *earnestly* to consider: that God did *not* create a specific Hell or place of torment on purpose to plague his creatures—namely, angels and men. 54. 55. It is the same with the souls of humans if they do not attain the light of God. 56. We give the courteous reader to understand: that the [hellish] creatures—which are the devils and the damned souls—have *not only* four forms in the bond of their life; rather, the forms are infinite, like the thoughts of humans. They can turn themselves into the forms of all creatures, but only four forms are *manifest* to them, as is also the case in the Abyss of Hell. They may bring forth *every* form out of the *Matrix* <note>original: "Matrix," the generative womb or source of nature</note> except the light. Fire is their proper life, and the sour harshness of the darkness is their proper food.

In this impregnation, the center of Nature consists; there would be no *Word* if there were no *Nature*.

80. For the *Word* takes its origin in Nature. We want you to understand very clearly that *two words* are generated in Nature. *One* is the first center of the Generating Mother, within the stern wrath. This expresses the strong power of the Mother of the first four forms of wrathfulness in the fire. This is called the Nature of God the Father, which he generates in this way within his quiet joy, in the conception of his will, without disturbing the Liberty of the Light.

<meta>This page continues Jacob Böhme’s exploration of the "Genetrix" (the Producing Mother), the process by which divine nature manifests. # Further regarding the Producing Mother <note>original: "Genetrix"</note>. Chapter 2.

[The Brightness, Glory, or Majesty] of the Father is *revealed*, which otherwise (in the first Will within the Dark Nature) appears only as *Fire*. But in the second Center, [it appears] as Love in the Light; and here Love and Enmity ought to be considered, along with how they oppose one another.

86. For Love is the death of wrathfulness, and by its shining, it takes away the power of that wrath. Here, the power of God in both Love and Anger is to be rightly understood.

87. The reason Love can be generated in this way is because of the first Will from the quiet dwelling place. For the quiet and clear dwelling, which is without a source <note>original: "source," often used by Böhme to mean an active, driving, or agonizing quality</note>, desires no fierceness, and yet it causes fierceness. If the fierceness did not exist, there would be no sharpness; consequently, the second Center (of Love) would not be generated either. It is from this center that the supernatural light shines, where the Names of God the Father and God the Son then exist.

88. For if Eternal Liberty <note>Böhme uses "Liberty" to describe the divine state beyond or before the constraints of Nature</note> did not generate the Being of Nature, there would be no Father, but merely nothingness. But since it does generate the Being of Nature, the Generator from which it is produced is called the Father.

89. Thus, the *Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness does not comprehend it,* as John says. In this way, Light and Darkness are opposite to one another, forming an Eternal Bond where one would not exist without the other. Here we must correctly consider the enmity against the power of the Light of God, and how each of them takes its origin.

90. For the Darkness *holds* four fierce qualities in its Center: stinging anguish in the sulfurous spirit; woe in the flash of fire; great fire in the "Breaking Wheel" <note>The "Breaking Wheel" or "Wheel of Nature" is Böhme’s term for the agonizing, revolving motion of the first forms of nature before they find the light</note>; and the rising of the essences in the flash of the power of the fire. Yet there is no escaping it; instead, it causes a will [to fly out or escape], and that is a Spirit. It is the *Bond of Nature* which God the Father generates in his Will, through which he reveals himself in the Eternal *Stillness*. Otherwise, there would be nothing. In this state, *God the Father* (with his power and fiery sharpness) is *an angry, zealous, jealous God, and a consuming fire.*

<margin>The seventh seal is the Holy Ternary <note>The "Holy Ternary" refers to the divine manifestation of the Trinity in a completed, "bodily" or spiritual state.</note></margin>
91. Let this be shown to you, oh you *Philosophers*; which (by the counsel of God) is opened to you in the Seventh Seal: in the *Holy Ternary* <note>original: "Ternario sancto"</note>.

92. Thus, the fountain of Love is a clasping and keeping in of the fierce wrath—indeed, it is an overcoming of that fierce power. For *Meekness* takes away the quality of the fierce, fourfold, hard power of the Fire; and the *Light* of that Meekness holds the Darkness captive and dwells in the Darkness [without being understood or contained by the Darkness].

94. Let this be a light to you, O you theologians <note>original: "Theologists [or Divines]"</note>: consider the writings of the saints *more correctly*, and behold the wonders of God with new eyes. Consider what God is in both Love and Anger, and observe how *two principles* stand open, each one desiring its own. If you wish to know God, a different kind of earnestness <note>original: "Earnest [or Zeale]"</note> must be used [rather than simply making formal conclusions in councils and synods]. You must go out from y Babel <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to represent the confusion of competing religious dogmas and empty intellectualism</note>, so that you may reach the Center of the Son of God. In this way, you shall be *born* [or generated] in meekness and in love. Only then may you feed the sheep of Christ; otherwise, you are thieves and murderers who step into the center of fierce wrath, where you do nothing but devour the sheep of Christ by fanning the flames of hellish fire. Oh, how falsely you deal with Love! How will you appear when the sun rises and you must stand in the Light? It shall hereafter be set before your eyes.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'A' decorated with intricate floral and foliate scrolls.</image-desc>

1. AND now, if we are to dive into the blessed *Birth of Love* and search out how it is generated and where it has its origin, we must search the center within. Let us set the *sixth form of nature* before us—namely, *Mercury* <note>In Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the "word," "sound," or "vibration" that brings life and expression to the forms of nature</note>—in which the *sound* [ringing or noise] is generated. In this study of the *generating* of Love, we shall find the tune, sound, and song, as well as the *five senses*: *sight*, *hearing*, *smell*, *taste*, and *touch*. Within these, life is understood, as are pain and torment, joy and love, and the desire for both good and evil. Although in the context of nature itself, nothing is to be rejected [or is in vain]; both good and evil must exist, otherwise God would not be manifested and all would remain as a *still nothingness*. The whole of Being exists together in the Eternal God; no one else has made or generated anything for Him. He alone, in His Eternal Will (which...

In the word *Ternarius* <note>original: "Ternarius"; a term referring to a group of three, representing the Trinity manifested within the material or natural realm</note>, one should rightly understand, according to the *Language of Nature* <note>the mystical idea that the sounds of words reflect the true essence of the things they name</note>, the Divine Birth within the six forms in Nature, which are the *six seals of God*.

18. But when I say *Holy Ternary* <note>original: "Ternarius Sanctus"</note>, I mean the number Three within *Seven Forms*, which encompasses the angelic world that exists in the seventh Birth. This is understood not according to the [pronunciation of] the *Latin tongue*, but according to the [pronunciation of] the *Language of Nature*. From this language, all things have received their *names*, which our *philosophers* in the schools of the *Third Principle* <note>the material, visible world</note> of this world do not understand; [but the *Theosophers* <note>those who seek direct knowledge of God and the cosmos</note> of the *School of Pentecost* <note>those enlightened by the Holy Spirit</note> understand it well].

19. For when I speak of the *Wrath* and of the *Anger of God*, I do not mean anything that exists *outside of God*; nor do I mean the pure *Deity* itself, which is unchangeable and in eternity is nothing else but Good, and is *not Nature*. Instead, the *Word* is generated out of the Nature of the Father as another or second *sprout* <note>or branch</note>, which is not contained within Nature; and therefore it is even another *Person*, and yet is generated out of the *First*.

<margin>* Conduct <note>original: "Wandel"</note>, communion, or conversation.</margin>
20. Understand that the first Will, which exists without Nature, is *free from Nature*, but Nature is generated within its *desire*. Therefore, the second Will (which goes forth out of the first, out of Nature as its own proper center) is also *free from Nature*. For it dwells in the first Will, which is called *Father*, in the *bright eternity*. It is the radiance [or *brightness*], power, strength, and being of the *bright eternity*; otherwise there would be no being within it, but only a still, light-filled habitation without existence or * *operation* <note>activity or working</note>.

This Word is the power and virtue, the heart, the life, and the being of the still eternity.

22. And since it is generated out of the *seven seals or forms of Nature*, it is therefore the *Maker and Creator* of all things out of the *being of Nature*. ### Chapter 3: Concerning the Birth of Love

...broke the seven seals of the fierce wrath and kindled the *Light* (which overcomes death and anger) in the soul.

58. It is not that the soul was *torn out* from the Father’s essences, as if it were no longer within the seven spirits of nature. No, that cannot be; everything remains within the seven spirits of the Father’s nature—even the Heart of God itself is positioned there. Rather, only the seals of death in the fierce wrath are *broken open* by the Light of the Heart of God in the *center* of the human soul.

59. For this, we thank God the Father in *Jesus Christ*, who became man and regenerated us in him toward the Light, redeeming us from the fierce, wrathful source [or torment] in the zeal of his anger throughout eternity.

<margin>u Accept or embrace.</margin>
60. But because we humans did not <gloss>u</gloss> accept such great grace and light, nor did we value it, but were instead pleased with the flesh of *Adam* and the desires of *this world*—and though we indeed saw that God performed great wonders and miracles in the man Christ, as well as in his disciples and all those who earnestly clung to him in the New Regeneration—we ourselves removed our *candlestick* and lived in hypocrisy. We lived in our own perceived holiness and in tyranny, and even persecuted Christ. Therefore, he also left us sealed up, so that we knew his Light no more. Instead, we sought out our own ways to God and tried to reach him through *our own* manufactured opinions. 
<margin>x Was more pleasing to us.</margin>
The kingdom of *this world* <gloss>x</gloss> was more pleasing to us than the kingdom of God. We practiced nothing but hypocrisy before him, and our hearts were far from him. Therefore, in the nature of the Father, we must remain under the seals until the spirit *Mercurius* <note>In Boehme’s thought, Mercurius represents the active, moving spirit of nature which, in the context of God's anger, acts as a "consuming fire."</note> [that is, the wrathful spirit in the anger of God, according to which God calls himself a *consuming fire*] has revealed all its wonders in us.

<margin>y Upon or among us.</margin>
61. And the *Book of Revelation* shows very clearly how the spirit *Mercurius* has opened one seal after another and has poured out all plagues and abominations <gloss>y</gloss> upon us. It has brought forth mere contention, wars, and malice—nothing but cunning, crafty subtlety, deceit, and falsehood—along with wonders and powers within us. Indeed, the scripture very accurately portrays us as an abominable beast, *like a dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns*.

91. But if you desire to enter the Temple of Christ, you must bring a humble, contrite, and broken heart with you, which earnestly longs for the Kingdom of God. It must not consist of hypocrisy, where people show themselves in a holy and devout posture while the poor soul is left outside the Temple of Christ in the seven spirits of darkness <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, the "seven spirits" or "properties" are the fundamental forces of nature and spirit</note>. In such a case, the person is a Christian in name only, while the heart is in doubt or else in the mere cravings of the flesh.

<margin>q Or, Actions.</margin>
92. O you blind sophisters <term>sophister: a person who uses clever but false arguments, especially a professional debater or academic theologian</term>! What have I to do with you, that I must write of your <gloss><sup>q</sup></gloss> strange acts? I have not sought your ways, but I have sought the Heart of God, so that I might hide myself in Christ. I desired only, like the Virgin in the *Book of Revelation* (*who stands upon the moon*), to fly into the *wilderness* away from the Dragon; and yet I myself must now point out the Dragon. LORD! You do whatever You will; Your ways are pure wonders.

<summary>Böhme critiques the divisive and judgmental nature of the institutional church ("Babel"), contrasting it with the internal "Temple of Christ" accessed through humility. He argues that true spiritual power comes from love and unity, as seen in the Apostles, rather than theological conflict.</summary>

## The Fourth Chapter.

1. When we thus show you the way of the Light, the Spirit is pleased not to speak merely as in a history, but to set forth the Light in its highest depth—in its wellspring or fountain—so that you might look, as if through an opened seal, into the *Holy Ternary* <note>original: *Ternarium Sanctum*; Böhme's term for the divine manifestation or the three-fold being of God in a substantive form</note>, [or the Eternal Essentiality].

2. Because the hidden mystery of the Kingdom of God shall be revealed in the seventh seal <note>A reference to the Book of Revelation, signifying a final age of total spiritual revelation</note>, and the Lamb himself shall be Shepherd over the sheep, it must *not be sealed up*. For we have known the voice of the trumpet of the seventh seal in the *Holy Ternary* <note>original: *Ternario Sancto*</note>, and therefore we may well speak of our native country, toward which our labor [or journey] tends.

3. No one should suppose us to be ignorant because we write so very deeply; for if we did not see and know it, we would have to remain silent. It is a common saying: *What the heart is full of, the mouth speaks.* This [which we have written] was not sought by this hand; but it is written: *I am found by those who did not seek me, neither did they inquire after me.*

4. I was as simple concerning the hidden mysteries as the lowest of all; but my Virgin of the Wonders of God <note>Böhme's personification of Divine Wisdom (Sophia), whom he describes as his spiritual guide and the mirror of God's wonders</note> taught me, so that I must write of His wonders. Although my purpose is indeed to write this as a *memorandum* <note>original: *Memorandum*; a note or record intended for future use</note> for myself, I shall still speak as if for *many*, which is known to God.

5. And now, as we are to speak of the seventh form of Nature, we see that corporeity <note>the state of having a physical body or substance</note> especially exists within it. For a spirit is empty [or raw] without a body, and there is no understanding without a body; moreover, the spirit itself does not exist without a body. For a form in the spirit is a hunger and a longing desire of one form after another.

<margin>r Or, do not intend.</margin>
<margin>s The work or deeds.</margin>
6. For all things exist in the will and are driven by the will; for if I have [or <insert>r</insert> *conceive*] no will to go, my body stands still. Therefore, my will carries me, and if I have no desire toward a place, then there is also no will in me. But if I desire anything, then that is the will of the <insert>s</insert> essences <note>original: "Essences"; Böhme uses this to describe the fundamental forces or qualities—like heat, light, or contraction—that constitute the "being" of a thing</note>.

### Of the Wellspring of Light. Chapter 4.

...seen that each form of the Spirit desires the other in its hunger. When that desire is attained, another (or second) form arises out of it. Yet the first form does not vanish; instead, the second form shapes itself within the first into another quality or property. Even so, both remain within one another, each keeping its own property. We have written regarding Nature in six forms: how one proceeds from the other, how one causes the other to be generated, and yet how each keeps its own property within the other. There they now stand, six forms within one another.

8. Thus, there is no place of rest, but rather a constant desire among all six forms. This is like a hunger from which the "will" is continually generated. Yet there is nothing in which rest can be found except for the still Eternity. However, this Eternity cannot be grasped or found within the "Wheel" of the fiery essences <note>The "Wheel of Nature" refers to the restless, cyclical movement of natural forces before they find spiritual balance.</note>. Therefore, hungry Nature seeks its "Mother" (that is, the desire of the harshness <note>original: "sourenesse," a term describing the contracting, astringent quality of the first property of nature</note>). This harshness catches hold of the desire of the essences and holds it fast. In this way, all the essences of hunger are held in the "Sour Mother," for she is their only rest; they, in turn, fill her with what is in them—that is, with themselves.

9. The dominion of a spirit consists in this: Nature does not consist of only seven forms. Instead, a new will can be generated out of every desire, and within that will, the essences exist again—though they are changeable according to the desire of that specific will. In this, there is no set number, as you can see in the creation of the world.

<margin>A mark or set limit.</margin>
10. However, because the Eternal Essence desires a certain limit or boundary—beyond which it does not wish to go, rise higher, or become anything else—the Heart generates itself. This Heart is the end-goal of Nature and the fulfillment of the Eternal Being <note>original: "Beeing, Essence, or Substance"</note>.

11. This Heart cannot be understood or grasped by Nature. Instead, Nature remains within its own darkness, and the Heart remains within its own light. Neither would be revealed without the other, and yet there is a continual hunger in both, for both Light and Darkness have worked from eternity.

<margin>Or, essential.</margin>
<margin>The physical body.</margin>
12. Now we see, in both the angelic world and this world, that the seventh form of Nature is a substantial <margin>u</margin> form, from which the existence of physicality <margin>x</margin> proceeded "by the word 'Let it be'" <note>original: "per verbum Fiat"; the divine command of creation from Genesis.</note>. We have searched the depths and find that this physical reality also exists in two forms: one in the darkness and the other in the light. Yet they do not belong to the actual "birth" of the darkness or the light; rather, they are the "body" or the physical manifestation <term>comprehensibility</term> <note>That which can be perceived or grasped by the senses.</note>.

13. We demonstrate this to you in terms of *Light* and *Darkness*. We cannot say that the *Darkness* is the *source* <note>original: "source [ or Property ]"</note>, but rather the *Darkness* <sup>y</sup> surrounds the property. It causes a property of *Anguish*—born from *longing* and *desiring*—to be <term>generated</term> within it. For although *Darkness* itself has no desire, the *desiring* is produced within it because the *Darkness* provokes it. Namely, a desire is conceived to be free from the *Darkness*. Therefore, the *desiring* labors so eagerly after this *liberty* until the *Anguish* within that *sharp desiring* <sup>z</sup> notices the *liberty* within itself. Yet at that stage, it is not yet truly called the *Liberty*, even though it is so. Instead, it exists in the *sharpness* of the *Anguish* and is called *Fire*. At this point, the *desiring* can go *no higher*; it must be *quenched* within itself and must *sink down* into the property.

# Chapter 4: Of the Wellspring of Light

60. For the mind does not stop searching until it comes to the innermost ground, which is shown *here*. Therefore, we would have the reader warned not to joke with these high, hidden mysteries; for by doing so, the Spirit of God is blasphemed.

He *wanted to dominate the Heart of God with his own self-will, wit, and reason*; he wanted God to be in subjection under him, and he wanted to be the framer and creator in nature; therefore, he became a devil.

89. And since I am generated out of the Nature of God, it is my *Mother* and the food of my soul; and my soul is the food of God. 90. I speak not only of myself, but of *all people* and *creatures* in whom His wonders are revealed, both in His love and His anger. For even the *devils* themselves exist within the wonders of God, as they reveal the *Seals of His Anger*; everything exists for the joy and glory of God.

11. There you see the seventh spirit of the divine nature, which is the joy of the *Majesty* of God, in which the *Trinity* manifests itself. There you see the *true angelic world*. For the sea is the water-spirit, which in the origin of nature is the fierce bitterness <note>original: "sourenesse"; in Boehme's system, this refers to the harsh, contracting first property of nature</note>. But it receives a shriek [or flash of light] from the light of God, which causes *this* harsh form to pass away. The shriek in the darkness turns into a sinking down into death; yet the captured shriek in the light (which is now called joy) is also a sinking down and is turned into *meekness*, in which the light shines. And it is like a glassy sea.

15. Behold, you seeking mind! I will show this to you even more deeply and clearly. Nature is generated out of the Father's original will, which in itself is only a Spirit and a darkness, yet it is driven by the will into seven forms—and out of those seven, into infinite forms. But the cause of Nature consists in the first four forms: namely, in the sour or harsh desire; in the *bitter sting*; in the *flash* of fire where life takes its origin; and the fourth in the *shriek* <note>original: "skreeke"; a sudden shudder or cry marking the transition from darkness to light</note> of the **Womb** <note>original: "Matrix"</note> before the fire. This is where the sinking of heavy death downwards and the rising of the fire-life upwards are generated. The *Center* then stands in the middle, like a heart in the body, out of which the **Tincture** <term>Tincture</term> (the fifth form of fire) arises, which is the desire for love. That desire is a penetrating *noise* or sound in the sixth form; and the life of the **Tincture** penetrates through the sinking down of death. This is where we understand the *meekness* of the **Tincture**, which makes that which is sinking down become physical or "corporeal," which is the seventh form. Out of this physicality in the beginning of this world, the Earth, stones, metals, and the whole center of the globe of the Earth were generated. The globe of the Earth, with its governance, stands in the six forms of Nature, while the seventh form is the *comprehensibility* or tangibility, as seen in Earth and stones. It is the body of the six forms, in which they perform their work like a spirit in the body. And the upper globe in the Deep above the Earth has just such a governance in seven forms: where the four elements maintain the upper center; and the constellations maintain the wheel of the essences of the Will; and the Sun maintains the **Tincture** of fire, in which every life in this outward world consists.

16. And just so is the *inward* governance in the **Holy Trinity** <note>original: "Ternario sancto"</note>. It is not severed from this world, but this world is severed from it only by a "principle" <note>Boehme uses "principle" to describe different dimensions or levels of reality that occupy the same space but operate differently</note>. For there is no corner or place in this world where the inward governance is not present.

### Chapter 5: And the Angelic World.

23. And although we have no tongue here that can (according to our *outward* language) bring these hidden mysteries to the *understanding*, yet we speak as a child to its mother. For the mother <note>original: "Mother." This is a reference to Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, whom Boehme describes as the spiritual source and nurturer of the soul.</note> has taken up our mind, and our sense sinks down into her *bosom*; where then we see in the light and know our mother, and speak thus of our mother’s house and of her food [ *on which we live* ].

24. And though we cannot well speak the language, yet we know it in our inner sense *very well*; and the reason why we do not have that language is because (according to the outward man <note>original: "outward Man." The physical, temporal self that belongs to the material world.</note>) we are altogether a stranger in our mother’s house. For the outward man does not belong to that house, and therefore it does *not* have the mother’s tongue [or language], but speaks with the *sense* of the inward man, which reaches to the mother.

<margin>u From.</margin>
25. Therefore here we shall be as it were dumb to those who are not born of God; for (according to the outward man) we are in this world, and according to the inward man, we are in God. Therefore the sense of the mind speaks of the kingdom of heaven, and the *outward spirit* (which is generated from the principle of this world) speaks <sup>u</sup> *from this world*, and the *inward* [spirit] (born of God) speaks <sup>u</sup> *from the inward world*.

26. Since then we are generated out of *both* worlds, we therefore speak in *two* languages; and so we must be understood also by *two* languages: one of which will despise this [work] and the other will highly believe and love it. For every spirit takes its own [just as the spider takes poison and the bee takes honey; the corrupt *Adam* (in *Ishmael*) loves scorning; the true man (in *Christ*) with *Isaac*, loves obedience].

27. But seeing that we are with our soul (in this world) in a strange lodging, and yet we certainly know that we must travel either into heaven to God or into hell to the devil; and since we do not like the devil, we would do well to seek after the kingdom of heaven and to cast our mind and thoughts upon *it*. For by doing so, we gain the precious crown of pearls instead of the *crown of this world* which the devil has set upon us through *sin*. With that crown, we go about in this world with brave shows, in hypocrisy, in arrogance <note>original: "high-mindednesse."</note>, and in our own authority and power; and therefore we will let those things go and speak of our *mother’s crown* in our native country.

28. We have sufficient understanding of *it* if we *know ourselves* aright, and we find it in our body and soul—as also in the form and shape of the body, but especially in the *mind*. But the spirit of this world does not know itself, unless another light shines in it, in which the mind can see and know itself.

29. For the *Spirit* born of *God* (which goes forth from *God* in the *Divine sense* [or understanding]) opens the mind to understanding and knowledge. In this way, a person sees themselves in the bonds <note>original: "Bands"</note> of this world; yet they do not see their own glory [there]. Instead, they look into the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: *Ternarium Sanctum*. In Boehme's theology, the "Ternary" represents the holy manifestation of the Trinity in the spiritual world.</note>, into the *Angelic* world for which they labor with great longing, and there is a continual restlessness within them.

30. For he is attracted by two: namely, by the *Spirit* of *God*, and by the *Devil*, in whose bonds he is also tied according to the outward sinful man. His center stands directly upon the *Cross*, and he is in this world like a *balance*, where one side goes suddenly up and then suddenly down again; we are here only in a valley of misery, anguish, and perplexity.

31. Now, seeing God is *so near us*, even within ourselves, let us seek him. If we wish to find him, we must turn away from this world and become like a little *infant* who is without understanding [of worldly things] and only clings to its *mother’s* breasts. We must be *newly born* in *God* with our minds and thoughts, or else we cannot see him; and *Christ* himself teaches us the same, saying *that his light shines in us.*

32. We must wholly reject our own *reason* and ignore the deceptive, flattering skill <note>original: "Art." Here meaning intellectual cleverness or worldly philosophy.</note> of this world. It is not sufficient to help us *to that Light*; rather, it is a mere leading astray and a holding of us back.

33. We point this out to the reader so that he may know [what it is that] he reads: [it is] not the *writing* of a *man* of worldly understanding, but of a *child*. Just as a *child* [newly born] from the *mother* is a stranger to this world [and has no understanding of it], so is this work written.

34. Therefore we speak of our child-like birth in **God**, for our beginning is upon the *Cross*. We are created upon the *Cross* as to our soul, and therefore the *body* also is a *Cross*. The center (namely, the *heart*) is in the middle of the *Cross*. With *Adam*, we have gone forth from the *image of the Cross* into the *image of the serpent*; but the *Son of the Virgin* [Jesus] has regenerated us again on the *Cross* into a heavenly image.

35. Therefore we will speak of what we see and know in the **Ground** <note>original: "Ground" (German *Grund*). This refers to the essential, underlying reality of God's nature.</note>, and we will not be silent. For a *Cross-birth* keeps its center in the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: *Ternario sancto*</note>. Understand this rightly: it is in the holy number Three, but not in the Majesty which is without Essence <note>Boehme distinguishes between the "unmanifest" God and the "manifest" God who exists as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.</note>. It is in the *distinction* of the Trinity where the Deity is called **Father, Son, and Holy Spirit**, where the two principles—the *Holy and the Wrathful*—separate. It is there that the flash <note>original: "flash." Boehme’s term for the sudden breakthrough of light and life out of the "fire" of God’s nature.</note> makes a *Cross*, and upon the *Cross*, the heart of God is generated [from eternity].

## The Gates of This World
### [Also concerning <unclear>the Language</unclear> of Nature]

79. Reason always asks: From what were the Earth and stones, as well as the elements and <margin>e Or, constellations.</margin> stars, generated? That is, it is not awakened or ignited by the kindling <note>The 'kindling' refers to the moment nature is moved from potentiality into active, sometimes violent, existence.</note>. It remains as it was from eternity and is not altered. It is neither increased nor diminished; in the act of creation, nothing is added to it or taken away from it. This principle possesses the true spirit of wisdom and understanding, which has separated the fierce, wrathful principle from the meek principle, so that each has its own life awakened within it.

<margin>Or, jealousy.</margin>
<margin>Or, into being.</margin>

In the inward, it sprouts in angry jealousy with great wonders and powers, where all forms are at work. Therefore, in those creatures lie all wit and cunning, craft and cleverness, as seen in the **devils**, who bring to pass all wonders in the wrathful womb <note>original: "Matrix" — the generative source or origin of natural forces.</note>, as the histories of the world concerning the children of wrath testify.

116. In the outward, it sprouts through meekness with the power [and virtue] of life, which goes forth from the heart of God through the Spirit of God. That sprouting [or vegetation] is called **Paradise**, and it is a sprout within the children of God. Together with this, the soul also sprouts; for in this sprouting, the new body of the soul grows in the [one] element—in substantiality—before the Threefold Spirit in the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: "Ternario sancto" — the divine realm of the Trinity.</note>.

<margin>Or, is.</margin>

It bleats and barks according to the form of the *out-birth* <note>The physical manifestation or external result of internal spiritual forces.</note> of the four *elements*, and has *no* higher *spirit* than the *elements* are. Though their fleeting senses [ <gloss>or perceptions</gloss> ] come from the ^f *constellations*, these are nonetheless dumb [ <gloss>or inarticulate</gloss> ^g ] and without comprehension of any substance.

5. Now, therefore, we will set before you the *foundation* <note>original: Ground</note> of the *heavens*, the *stars*, and *elements* *fundamentally*, so that you may see what is *heavenly* and what is *earthly*; what is *transitory* and *mortal*, and what is *eternal* and *permanent*. We have intended to write this *book* for this purpose *alone*: *not* to boast of our high knowledge, which is in *God* and is of *no* worldly *profit* to us, but out of *love* in *Christ*, as a *servant* and *minister* of *Christ*, to seek the lost sheep of the *house* of the *Israel* of *God*.

6. For the *Lord* holds both the willing and the doing in his hands; we are able to do nothing. Also, our *earthly reason* understands nothing. We are yielded into our *mother’s bosom* <note>Likely referring to Divine Wisdom or the "Mother" of all things in Boehme's theology.</note> and do as the *mother* shows us. We know nothing of any other source; we are not born with it from the wisdom of this world, nor do we understand it. But what is bestowed upon us, that we bestow again. We have no other purpose here, nor do we know to what end [ <gloss>we must write these high things</gloss> ], but merely what the *spirit* shows us, that we set down.

26. Or do you not know what **Christ** said concerning the two **Sons**? When the father said to one of them, "Go and do such a thing," and he said he would, and the other said no. The other, who was under the name of obedience [or who in word was obedient, or had the reputation of being so], did not do it.

27. And we are all such, one and another; we bear the name of Christ and are called Christians, and are within his Covenant. We have said yes, we will do it; but those who do it not are **unprofitable servants** and live outside the will of the Father.

# Chapter 6: Of the World and of Paradise

31. If we consider ourselves according to our true nature—as a true likeness and image of God—then we find God within us, and yet we find our external selves existing outside of God. The only remedy consists of this: that we enter again into our inner selves and enter into God through our *hidden self* <note>original: "hidden Man"; a biblical and mystical term referring to the inner spiritual life (1 Peter 3:4)</note>. If we direct our wills with true, earnest sincerity toward God, then we go with Christ out of this world, away from the influence of the stars and the elements, and enter into God. For in the will of human reason, we are children of the stars and elements, and the *spirit of this world rules over us*.

32. But if we leave the will of this world and enter into God, then the *Spirit of God rules within us* and establishes us as his children. Then also the *crown of Paradise* <note>original: "Garland of Paradise"</note> is placed upon the soul, and it becomes like a child without understanding regarding this world; for the soul loses the Master (or Ruler) of this world, who previously ruled and guided it through human reason.

33. O humankind! Consider who leads and drives you; for **eternity without end is very long**. Temporary honor and possessions are but dross and dung in the sight of God. All of it falls into the grave with you and comes to nothing. But to be within the will of God is **eternal riches and honor**. There, there is no more worry, for our Mother <note>In this context, the "Mother" refers to Divine Wisdom (Sophia) or the eternal essence of God's love.</note> cares for us, and we live in her bosom like children.

<margin>A pitfall, trap, or snare.</margin>
34. Your temporary honor is your snare, and your suffering endured with divine hope and confidence is your garden of roses. Patience is a precious herb. Oh, how gloriously you will be crowned! What is brighter than the **sun**? And yet you shall be far brighter. You will obtain a crown in the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: *Ternario Sancto*; this refers to the "Holy Trinity" manifested in eternal substance or the angelic world.</note>.

<margin>Or, lulled asleep.</margin>

We do not boast of this, for the power belongs to the Mother; but we encourage you to enter into the bosom of the Mother and learn also to see with **your own eyes**. As long as you allow yourselves to be lulled asleep in a cradle and desire to see through the eyes of **others** (which are foreign eyes compared to your own), you are blind. But if you rise up from the cradle and go to the Mother, then you shall see the Mother and her children.

36. Oh, how good it is **to see with one’s own eyes**! 37. So also I say, we are all asleep in the outward Man; we lie in the cradle and allow ourselves to be *rocked asleep* by *Reason*. We see with the eyes of the deception of our *Hypocrites*, who hang bells and *baubles* <note>original: "Bables"; trinkets or toys used to distract a child</note> about our ears and cradles, so that we may be lulled asleep, or at least play with their *baubles*, so that they may be *Lords* and *Masters* in the *House*.

38. O *Blind Reason*! Rise up from your *cradle*. Are you not a *Child* of the *Mother* <note>Referring to Divine Wisdom</note> and an *heir* to the *Goods*? Moreover, are you not a *Child* and *Lord* of the *House*? Why do you allow *your* servants to use you this way? We should see (with *inner eyes*) in his *Light*, and so we should see him, for he is the *Light*. When we see him, then we walk in the *Light*. He is the *Morning Star*, and he is born in us, and rises in us, and shines in our bodily *darkness*.

39. O, how great a *Triumph* there is in the soul when he arises! Then a person sees with *his own eyes* and knows that he is in a strange lodging. Concerning this, we will write here what we see and *know* in the *Light*.

40. We are children of *Eternity*, but this world is an out-birth <note>original: "outbirth"; a physical manifestation or derivation from a spiritual source</note> of the *Eternal*. Its tangibility takes its origin in the *Anger* <note>original: "Anger"; in Boehme’s cosmology, this refers to the "wrathful" or stern quality of the divine nature that provides the necessary friction or "fire" for material existence</note>; the *Eternal Nature* is its root. But that which is an out-birth is corruptible because it has not existed from eternity, and it must all return into the *Eternal Essence* from which it was born.

<margin>ᵈ Or, caused by the wrestling wheel.</margin>

Therefore, they are so various and numberless to our reckoning. Though indeed there is a certain number of them, by which we know that they must enter again into the *Ether* <note>The "Ether" here refers to the refined, spiritual substance from which the stars were thought to be composed</note>.

42. For in the Eternal Center there is no number [or measure], but it is the *Omnipotence* springing up without number. For that which cannot be numbered or comprehended is not *Eternal*; it has a beginning and an end. But we know that the *Spirit* and soul of man has no beginning and no end, nor can it be numbered [or measured]. We understand this by the *constellations* of the *mind*, from which so many thoughts arise, which are numberless; for out of one *thought* in a short while, many may go forth...

43. <margin>e Or, observe this well here.</margin> Understand us correctly: how this world exists in its base and foundation. The eternal center, the birth of life, and physical substance are everywhere. If you make a small circle, as small as a tiny <margin>f As small as a mite, a point, or an atom.</margin> grain [or kernel of seed], the whole birth of eternal nature is there, along with the Trinity in the *holy ternary* <note>original: "Ternario sancto"; a Latin term referring to the holy three-fold manifestation of God within the created substance</note> [contained] within it. Eternal nature is incomprehensible, just as God is.

44. When I take up anything and carry it away, I do not carry away eternity, much less God. Yet eternity is in that very thing; however, the thing is <margin>g Born out <note>original: "Exgeneratum"</note></margin> *born out* of it and does not disturb eternity. That which is born out does not contain eternity, but eternity contains that which is born out completely, without being moved. For eternity, as also the Deity, is in one place as well as in another [everywhere]. There is no "place" [in eternity], but the "out-birth" (physical creation) creates place and space. Therefore God says: *I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end.*

45. This world has a beginning, and God in the Trinity [not without it] is that beginning. It also has an end, and that is eternity, which is also God. For before [the time of] this world, there was *nothing but God* from eternity; and after this world, there will be *nothing but God* in eternity. But the reason why we do not grasp this is because there is no way to limit or define God <note>original: "comprehensibility"; here meaning the quality of being contained or limited within boundaries that the human mind can grasp</note>. For where there is a limit [as there is in the Trinity], there is a beginning and an end. Therefore, we are enclosed in darkness so that we might work and *reveal* God. As we have mentioned to you concerning the Seven Forms of Nature <note>The author’s complex system of seven qualities or "fountains" that drive the process of divine manifestation</note>, there is an eternal labor *within them*, so that one form generates another until they are all brought to the Light. In this way, the eternal is revealed in a threefold form, which otherwise would not be known.

46. And we declare to you that the eternal being, and also this world, *is like man*. Eternity generates nothing but what is like itself, for there is nothing in it that is not like it, and it is unchangeable. Otherwise, it would <margin>h Or, cease to be.</margin> pass away or become *something else*, and that cannot happen.

# Of the World and of Paradise. Ch. 6.

...was again set in the Eternal Humanity, for the Word dwelt in Christ’s flesh and assumed the soul in him.

<margin>ⁿ A being or a thing.</margin>
86. It is not that the soul and the Word are one and the same ⁿ substance. No, the soul originates from the *Center of Nature*; it is generated out of the essences and belongs to the body, for it proceeds from the essences of the body and attracts corporeality <note>original: "corporeity"</note> to itself. But the Word originates from the *Center of Majesty* and attracts majesty to itself.

87. The Word exists without substance, while the soul arises out of substance; it is the spirit of that substance, originating from the *Center* of the Father. Otherwise, in *Adam*, the soul could not have departed from the Word. This does not mean the Word and the soul stand side-by-side like two separate persons; rather, the Word penetrates through the soul. From the Word, the majesty shines forth—namely, the Light of Life. Yet the soul remains independent in itself, for it is a created thing.

<margin><insert>Ex: 104</insert></margin>
88. I will give you an earthly analogy <note>original: "similitude"</note> for this. Consider a bright, flaming piece of *iron*. By itself, the iron is dark and black, but the fire so penetrates and shines through it that it gives off light. The iron does not cease to be; it is still iron. Likewise, the nature <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> of the fire retains its own characteristics. It does not absorb the iron into itself but rather penetrates and shines through it. The iron remains iron, just as it was before, independent in its own nature. The same is true for the fire. This is how the soul is positioned within the Deity: the Deity penetrates the soul and dwells within it. Yet, the soul does not encompass <note>original: "comprehend"</note> the Deity; rather, the Deity encompasses the soul. It *does not change the soul’s fundamental nature*, but only imparts to it the divine quality <note>original: "source [or property]"</note> of majesty.

89. Therefore, if the soul inclines itself toward the divine quality, it remains within the majesty of God. This quality signifies the *Word*, and the radiance [*signifies the Majesty*]. That which proceeds from this quality—just as heat comes out of fire—signifies the *Holy Spirit*.

90. However, if that flaming iron is cast into water, the fire’s properties—the radiance and the heat proceeding from it—are all quenched at once. This is what happened with *Adam*. By his own will, he cast himself out from the majesty of God and into the spirit of this world; thus, he departed from God.

<margin>ᵒ Or, *was extinguished*.</margin>
<margin>ᵖ The radiance, luster, or majesty.</margin>
91. It is not that God ᵒ was extinguished within him, like the fire in the iron; no, that is impossible. ᵖ The divine light shines eternally. God remains within His own principle, but *Adam* stepped out of it. If *Adam’s* will had remained focused on God, he would have continued as a child of God. God would have remained in his will, and thus the divine majesty would have shone through his will.

<summary>Boehme explains the relationship between the soul and the Word of God using the analogy of heated iron, where the fire (God) penetrates the iron (the soul) without changing its fundamental nature. He argues that Adam's fall was a willful departure from this divine radiance into the spirit of the world.</summary>

92. But he turned away from the will of God and entered into this world; thus, he was captured by the *World, Death, Devils, and Hell*, and they took up residence in *Adam*.

93. *Adam* was in this world, living within the elements, and God breathed the *air* into his nostrils as well. However, he should not have directed his will toward it, nor should he have eaten of the *earthly fruit* which produces earthly flesh. 94. Then the Word of the Lord said to the soul, "*Adam*, where are you?" and his body hid itself. The poor soul was so deeply ashamed. *Adam* said, "I am naked." His soul then regains the Eternal Flesh in which God became man—an incomprehensible flesh of eternal substance.

<margin>q Or, Mortal Flesh.</margin>

98. This is the Noble Precious Stone, the *Philosopher's Stone* <note>original: "Lapis Philosophorum"</note>, which the *Magi* <note>original: "Magi [or Wisemen]"</note> find. He who finds this prizes it more highly than this [outward] world. For the son is many thousand times greater than the father.

Not that the soul and the Word are one and the same substance; no, the soul is from the Center of Nature <note>In Boehme's thought, the "Center of Nature" is the root of natural, temporal existence.</note>, generated out of the essences <note>original: "Essences"; the active qualities or spiritual "powers" of being.</note>, and it belongs to the body. For it proceeds from the essences of the body and attracts physical form <note>original: "Corporeity"</note> to itself. But the Word is from the Center of Majesty and attracts Majesty to itself.

87. The Word is without substance, and the soul is from substance; it is the spirit of the substance from the Center of the Father. Otherwise, in Adam, it could not have departed from the Word. It is not that the Word and the soul stand next to each other like two separate persons; rather, the Word penetrates through the soul. And from the Word, the Majesty shines—that is, the Light of Life. The soul is free in itself, for it is a creature.

<insert>28 : 264</insert>
88. I will give you an earthly illustration <note>original: "similitude"</note> of this. Imagine a bright flaming piece of iron which, by itself, is dark and black; the fire so penetrates and shines through the iron that it gives off light. Now, the iron does not cease to be; it is still iron. The source (or property) of the fire retains its own nature <note>original: "propriety"</note>; it does not turn the iron into itself, but it penetrates and shines through the iron. It is still iron, just as before, free in itself; and the same is true for the source (or property) of the fire. In this same way, the soul is placed within the Deity. The Deity penetrates through the soul and dwells in the soul, yet the soul does not contain <note>original: "comprehend"</note> the Deity. Rather, the Deity contains the soul, but does not change its nature as a soul; it only gives it the divine quality <note>original: "source" or "property"</note> of Majesty.

89. And so, if the soul inclines itself toward the divine quality, then it remains in the Majesty of God. For the source (or property) represents the Word, and the radiance <note>original: "Glance"</note> represents the Majesty; and that which proceeds from the source, like heat out of fire, represents the Holy Spirit.

90. But now, if the flaming iron is cast or falls into water, then the property of the fire—the radiance and the heat which proceed from it—are all quenched together. This is how it was with Adam: he cast himself out from the Majesty of God (by his own will) into the spirit of this world, and so he departed from God.

<margin>
o Or, was extinguished.
p The radiance, luster, or majesty.
</margin>

If Adam’s will had remained in God, he would have remained a child of God, and God would have remained in his will, and thus the Majesty would have shined through his will.
