# Of the True Cornerstone. Ch: 7.

<margin>The Noble Stone.</margin>
100. Christ says, *“Seek and you shall find.”* It must be sought for; a lazy person does not find it, and though he carries it about with him, yet he does not know it. To whomsoever it reveals itself, he has all joy in it, for there is no end to its power <note>original: "vertue"; in this context, it refers to inherent power, efficacy, or divine potency.</note> [or Glory]. He who has it does not give it away; and if he does share it with anyone, it is still not profitable to a person who is lazy, for such a person does not dive into its power to learn it.

101. But the seeker finds the Stone and its power and benefit together. When he finds it and knows that he is *certain* of it, there is greater joy in him than the world is able to understand—a joy which no pen can describe, nor any tongue express, in a human <note>original: "Adamical"; referring to the fallen state of humanity inherited from Adam.</note> manner.

102. It is accounted the *meanest* <note>original: "Meanest"; here meaning the most humble, insignificant, or lowliest.</note> of all stones in human eyes and is trodden underfoot, for it offers no luster to the sight. If a man happens upon it, he casts it away as a worthless thing. None inquire after it, though it is so very much sought for in this world. There is no one on Earth who does not desire it. All the great ones and the wise seek it; indeed, they find one and think it is the right one, but they miss it. They ascribe power and virtue to their find and think they have it and will keep it—but it is *not* that Stone. That Stone needs no virtue to be ascribed to it: *All power lies hidden within it.*

103. He who has it and knows it, if he seeks, he may find all things whatsoever are in Heaven and on Earth. It is the *Stone which is rejected by the builders and is the chief cornerstone; upon whatsoever it falls, it grinds to powder, and it kindles a fire within.*

<margin>High schools or academies.</margin>
All *universities* seek it, but they do not find it by *their* seeking; sometimes it is found by someone who seeks it rightly. But others [who seek it for themselves and for their own gain] despise it and cast it away, and so it remains hidden still.

<margin>1.</margin>
IT concerns us humans most of all in this world to seek that which is lost. And therefore, if we would seek, we must not seek outside of ourselves. We need no flattering hypocrites, nor those who tickle our ears to comfort us and promise us many mountains of gold if we will only run after them, fawning over them and revering them.

If a stone is cast into the *water* and then taken out again, it remains the same hard stone it was before and retains its ª nature. 3. Also, it is not enough for you to study all books so that you can recite them from memory, or to read all writings every day and year, or even to know the *whole Bible* by heart. 4. They forbid the Light to those who can see, just as has been done to this writer <note>original: "this hand"; the author is likely referring to the censorship or persecution he personally experienced.</note>. They *study first* to decide which "Opinion" they will use to enter the temple of Christ. Such a person sets men’s opinions before him and seeks God only within this or that *Opinion*: one in the ᵈ *Catholic opinion*, another in ᵉ *Luther’s*, a third in ᶠ *Calvin’s*, a fourth in ᵍ *Schwenkfeld’s*, and so on. You must forsake everything in this world (no matter how *glittering* it may seem) and enter into yourself, gathering only your sins (which have captivated you) together.

18. But that God should cast away the <term>Third Principle</term> <note>original: "Third Principle"; in Böhme's philosophy, this refers to the external, visible world of matter and time.</note> [that is, the Created World] for humanity's sake, and return it to its <term>Ether</term> <note>original: "Ether"; here meaning the primordial, non-material state or the "nothingness" from which the world was formed.</note> before its time is fulfilled, that cannot be. For the wonders that were foreseen from eternity in the Wisdom without substance must come to have a substance, and so, in time, the forms of Nature must also come to exist.

19. For God is threefold in Person, and intended to move himself three times, according to the property of each Person, and no more throughout eternity.

20. **First**, the center of the Father’s nature moved itself toward the creation of angels, and subsequently of this world.

21. **Secondly**, the Son’s nature moved itself, where the Heart of God became man—which shall never happen again in eternity. And where it is done now—meaning, where people become united with the Heart of God, as branches on their vine—it is done only through that one Man who is God, through many people, and in many people.

22. And **Thirdly**, the Holy Spirit’s nature will move itself at the end of the world, when the world shall enter into its ether again and the dead shall rise again. 64. You must understand us this way concerning the Eternal Being. The Eternal Being is like this, and if it were not, everything would be as *nothing*—nothing but an eternal stillness *without* existence <note>original: "Being"</note>. We find this to be true in everything.

65. Thus we may consider for ourselves where these wrathful and good wills arise. Now, the heat is Nature, and the light is the eternal liberty outside of [or beyond] Nature, for Nature does not contain <note>original: "comprehendeth"</note> the light.

66. In the same way, you must understand the two types of wills in God. The *one* is Nature; it is not called "God," and yet it belongs to God, for he is angry, severe, and sharp as a sting—consuming, attracting all things to himself, and devouring them. It is always striving to fly up above the light [which is the *other* will], and yet it cannot—just as fire does. The higher the fire flies, the higher the light goes, and so they may well be called *two principles*.

## The Eighth Chapter.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'N' featuring foliate and floral patterns.</image-desc>
1. Just as there is a life and spiritual government in the deep of the world in all places, so that all creatures are included as if in one body—which provides them with life, nourishment, wit, wisdom, and skill in all their kinds (in humans, beasts, birds, fishes, worms, trees, and herbs, each according to the kind of their internal qualities <note>original: "Essences"</note>)—so there is also a life in the eternity within this world which the spirit of this world does not comprehend. This eternal life has all the properties of this world within it, but not in such burning <note>original: "kindled"</note> qualities.

2. For it has no fire, though indeed it has a mighty fire, but it burns in another manner <note>original: "source or property"</note>—namely, *in the desiring*. It is soft, delicate, or pleasant, without pain; also, it consumes nothing. Instead, its Spirit is *love* and *joy*. Its fire creates *majesty* and brightness, and that has always been from eternity. It has no bottom <note>original: "ground"</note>; it has its own springing up and blossoming, but not out of the kind of earth we walk upon. And yet it is *Earth*, which throughout my book I call *Substantiality*, for it is the *Eternal Body* without any defect. There is no lack in it, nor sorrow, nor misery; no such thing is known there at all. There is no death, devil, nor anger known in it; instead, such things stand altogether in the darkness [or in eternal oblivion], hidden in the first principle.

<summary>This page describes the transition from the transitory physical world back to its eternal spiritual source, explaining that the forms of this world will remain as a joyful "picture" for eternal beings. It introduces the concept of a spiritual life and "Substantiality" (an eternal body) that exists within the world but is free from the pain and "fire" of material existence.</summary>

43. He [Lucifer] was a prince and a throne-angel, and was created with the *first* creation. Therefore, since he was a cause of the Third Principle (by which we mean the Out-birth <note>original: "Out-Birth"; in Boehme’s cosmology, this is the physical, external world that was "born out" of the spiritual realms</note>), Christ also called him a "prince of this world." We often <insert>make or</insert> do works that are contrary to God, only for the sake of our status and honor, as is seen in forts, castles, and <margin>* Palaces.</margin> sumptuous, great houses.

44. <margin>d For the place of this world would have burned in the fire for Lucifer.</margin>
45. That [awakened matrix of the fire] is now his *hell*, and God has captured that hell with heaven, namely <note>original: "viz."; short for the Latin "videlicet"</note> the matrix of the water. For [Lucifer desired] the place of this world <margin>d</margin> to burn in the fire for him [to domineer in]. Therefore, God moved himself to the Creation and did create; and so there was water, which captured his wrathful hell [just as the pleasant sun shuts out the harsh <note>original: "Astringent"</note> cold and turns ice into water, through which fish and other creatures grow and live].

<margin>e Where the great waters are.</margin>
46. And the cause of the sea and of the great, deep waters, whose bottom cannot be fathomed, is that the *matrix* of nature in <margin>e</margin> those places was so intensely ignited <note>original: "enkindled"</note> in the fire.

47. And here we give you an example of this. But when the devil thought he would be lord and have his habitation there, then God *broke* his pride and stubbornness <note>original: "Stoutnesse"</note> and caused water to cover that place, quenching his pride.

<margin>f Or, that the anger was kindled.</margin>
48. In this, we have an excellent example of God’s care for his children who depend on him; for when he saw the <margin>f</margin> wrath, he brought Lot out of Sodom. Furthermore, you have here a full example: when the wrath of God begins to be ignited, he makes it *known* to his children beforehand so that they might flee from it, just as he told *Abraham* and *Lot* and commanded them to flee. He has done so from the beginning of the world. For the prophets existed for no other purpose than to declare the *anger of God* and to command the children of God to flee from it, as may be seen by what was done to *Jerusalem* and the *Jewish nation*, and has always been done to *all people* from the beginning of the world to this time. 49. Therefore, let no one blindfold themselves, but consider what such a *warning* and *revelation* signifies, which is currently presented to the world. This is the time of the overthrow of the Dragon, along with the Whore of Babylon <note>original: Babell; a reference to the corrupt religious and political systems described in the Book of Revelation</note>, which shall go down into the abyss. Now, even for those who will not flee, let them be warned of it. He who brings the Whore's marks forth into the light will face great disgrace and reproach for it; we speak what we must. The day dawns and *the sun will suddenly arise*; do not consider it a fiction. It is decided and known in the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: Ternario Sancto; the divine manifestation of the Trinity within the created order</note>. Look into the Scriptures, specifically the **Book of Revelation**, which the sophists <note>deceptive or overly intellectual religious scholars</note> would rather have cast out of the Bible; but the understanding of it will soon *bud forth*. Then the peddlers of the Beast and of the Whore will stand in great shame, and no one will buy their wares anymore. *No sword destroys the Whore, but her own mouth chokes her*; for there are nothing but lies and blasphemies in it, and yet she acts as if she were God. Therefore we say, let everyone look to their own actions; lift up your heads, as Christ says, *for the time of your redemption draws near*. You are baptized with water; but he who will baptize with the Holy Spirit and with the fire of his wrath *is already on his way*. Do not be willfully blind.

<margin>& Solely, or alone.</margin>
50. Thus, understand us correctly concerning the life of man, as we have now mentioned: This last aforementioned life exists *& solely* in animals, for it has its origin only in the **principle** <term>Principle: a fundamental source or governing spiritual realm</term> of this world, in the **Matrix of Nature** <term>Matrix: the source or "womb" from which natural forms originate</term>, which is everywhere such a spirit and such a life in itself.

51. In man, life is twofold: for man also has the life of this [outward] principle in him; but he also desires another life, which is higher and better than this.

52. And now, where there is a desire, there is a "mother," who is the desire itself; for no desire can create itself—it must arise out of a will, and the will must come out of the **Tincture** <term>Tincture: the spiritual essence or life-force that gives a being its specific quality and vitality</term>, which is the life of the will.

53. Thus we know and have discovered that in the tincture of the principle of this world—that is <note>original: viz.</note>, in the life of this world—there is also *another tincture*, of which we have an awareness within ourselves. If there were not another tincture, the life would desire nothing more.

54. Yet we cannot say that the outward life desires anything more; it desires nothing else but its own mother—namely, the principle of this world. For it is only a spirit within it, as no principle desires another. A principle is a distinct life and has its own center of nature; therefore we call it a "principle," because there is a total dominion within it, just as there is in eternity.

58. The other desire in man after the highest Good is the soul, which stands in the Eternal Mother <note>the divine source or matrix from which all things are birthed</note>. For every desire has its origin out of its own Mother; therefore, this is a desire of Eternity—and not the Eternity itself, but the **Tincture** of Eternity and the **Majesty**, namely the glance in the Still Habitation, as has now been mentioned.

59. Now, if a spirit is in its own Mother, it does not desire to go out from her again [just as the air-spirit does not desire to go away from the body]. Neither does it desire **anything more** than what is in its Mother and in its Center.

60. But yet we find and understand it in our mind that the soul wills to be out of this [**Earthly**] Mother in which it stands at present. And not only so, but it desires the house of its own Mother—namely, its own **Tincture** and the Majesty, as well as the Eternal Rest out of the **Tincture**.

#### *Highly to be Considered.*

It is shown to me what the Devil's intention is: how he will endeavor to smother these high and precious writings. Therefore, be watchful, you children of God; *do not believe the sophisters* <note>original: "Sophifters"; in this context, it refers to academic theologians or those who use clever but deceptive arguments to maintain their status.</note> *too much*, who cry out, "Heretic, heretic, to the fire with them!" That is not the voice of the Holy Spirit, but the voice of the Antichrist and of the dragon. For these writings will thoroughly reveal the Devil’s smoking pit; and not only so, but they also show the *Whore of Babylon* <note>original: "Whore of Babell"; a biblical figure from Revelation used by reformers to symbolize religious corruption.</note> very plainly, like a whore <margin><sup>t</sup> Exposed in the pillory <note>original: "Am Pranger"; a German expression meaning to be publicly shamed or placed in a pillory.</note></margin> <sup>t</sup> put to open shame.

2. But (because the men of the spirit of this world take care *only* for their bellies, and are loath to lose their honor, credit, reputation, and goods, but would rather part with God and the kingdom of heaven), we shall be persecuted by the *Whore* through the instigation of the devils. Therefore, be watchful, you children of God, and do not look upon that which is high and has great authority, but regard the welfare of your souls. This we leave you as a last farewell.

3. No one ought to call themselves after *my name*; all of us who know Christ put him on and are members of *his body*. We call ourselves Christians and children of God, and brothers and sisters of one another.

We shall not mention that further here, for it belongs to the *Magi* <term>original: "Magi"; spiritually gifted individuals who understand the hidden mysteries of nature.</term> who are born *magically*. We speak only of the foundation of nature and of the Spirit of this world.

9. And we declare to you that the Spirit of this world is created with such an inclination, and that it has a natural will to reveal itself and all its *mysteries*. We see this before our eyes by what it has built or brought forth—how it has established a dominion and kingdom upon earth.

10. Just look at the actions of humanity, from the highest to the <margin>the course.</margin> lowest: the Spirit of this world has thus built the whole order of them, and God has permitted it. For God is not a destroyer, but a preserver of that which His power builds up, and He accounts it as *His ordinance*; for nothing is brought forth which has not existed in eternity.

11. But you must understand it correctly: Hell and Anger are the *Abyss*, which also mingles its wonders therein. We see this where <margin>Or, contrast [foyle].</margin> there is good ground, and the Sower also sows good seed, yet thistles and thorns grow up among it—just as *Christ* gave us a parable of the Sower. As it is in the mind of humanity, so it is also in the Spirit of this world.

12. You should know that all weeds, such as thistles and thorns, as well as serpents, toads, evil beasts, and worms, have their origin from the *Wrathful Matrix* <term>original: "Matrix"; the creative womb or source of nature.</term>. For at the time of Creation, everything, both good and evil, came forth—each according to its kind and property. There is good and evil in everything, and the Kingdom of Anger has also completely ª imprinted itself upon them; therefore, the fruit is both good and evil, and Adam should not have eaten of it.

13. I am teaching you, through the fruits of the earth, how good and evil exist within one another. Each has its own usefulness, the evil as well as the good. All serve to manifest God’s wondrous deeds, and each is useful to the spirit of this world. What one harms, the other heals, and that also is a wonder.

14. Furthermore, we see the *Mysterium Magnum* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"; Latin for "The Great Mystery," referring to the chaotic source or "chaos" from which the manifested world was created.</note>, the Great Mystery, in the trees. Although they are indeed diverse and mixed, we can still discern the *Paradisiacal* form [or condition] in them; for they bear their fruit upon twigs, and the fruit is something different from the tree. The tree is bitter, and the fruit is sweet. We want you to understand that the trees and fruit we have today would be *Paradisiacal* if the Curse did not cling to them. Paradise has fled from them, and now all fruit is *only such* as the apple was from which Eve ate death. You should also know that the Kingdom of Anger also pressed into the Garden of Eden, which brought forth a tree that bore the same kind of fruit as all the trees we eat from today.

<margin>b Mild or sweet.</margin>

Humanity does not naturally desire [to eat] the [first] essences of the earth, unless it is a very ᵇ pleasant herb; instead, we desire the *second birth* out of the earth—namely, the *kernel* [seed or fruit]. This is indeed the second birth from the earth, through which we understand our high origin. But before the Fall, Paradise *sprang up* through all trees and through all the fruits that God created for humanity.

Therefore, it is because of this that we eat death in all fruits, and the spirit [ᵈ of] evil and good rules in us. The spirit of this world rules in us, as does the Devil with the spirit of anger, and each of them displays their wonders in and through humanity.

### [*Of the Great Struggle for the Image of Man*]

17. There is a great struggle over the Image of Man <note>In Boehme's philosophy, the "Image of Man" refers to the original spiritual blueprint of humanity before the Fall.</note>; each kingdom wants to possess it. *Hell*, in the spirit of Anger, says: "It is mine by right of Nature; it is generated out of my root." The *Spirit of the world* also says: "I have it in my body, and I give it life and nourishment. I bring it up and give it all my powers and wonders; it is mine." And the *Kingdom of God* says as well: "I have set my heart upon it and have regenerated it; it has come out of my Kingdom. I have fought for it and found it again; it is mine, and it must reveal my wonders."

18. Thus, there is a fierce struggle within and concerning Man. Look at his conduct <note>original: "Conversation"; in the 17th century, this meant one's entire way of living or behavior.</note> and his actions: his desire stands especially in *three things*, and these are the three kingdoms which rule him. Whichever one he falls into, there he remains.

19. First, he desires power, honor, and glory, so that everyone might fear and honor him. This is the very poison of the Devil, who also has such an intention, which he satisfies by doing as much as he can.

20. Secondly, he desires riches, goods, and money, as well as much eating and drinking, and he does not care by what means he obtains them. This is the *Spirit of this world*, which desires only shelter and plenty, just as a beast does.

21. And thirdly, he also desires the Kingdom of Heaven; he desires and pants after it, but in great weakness. He is always in doubt, thinking that he is a sinner and that God does not want him. Yet he sighs and pants after it and would gladly be saved. He prays and yet doubts; he hopes and yet fears; he hopes for improvement and deliverance from one day to the next, always supposing it will be better tomorrow—that "tomorrow you will have the power to leave this way of life and enter another." It is always like this with him.

22. We are not speaking here about those who live like swine, who lie wallowing in the mire and never seek any improvement. Instead, we are speaking about the poor sinners caught between Heaven and Hell, who feel the attractions of both and yet are held back.

23. Yet observe what Man does: he *follows* all three of these desires. He continually seeks power and honor until his end; he continually hunts after greed, money, and goods to eat and drink; and even if he has more than enough, in his greed he never has enough. He acts as if he were to live here forever. And then, thirdly, he also pants after the Kingdom of Heaven, for the poor soul is very much perplexed and is always afraid of the...

### [*Of the Devil, who changes himself into an Angel of Light*]

24. They say the Devil comes to man in the form of an angel, and it is true. *Observe what he does* so that he is considered an angel and is thought to be good. When the poor soul is thus *disquieted* and often presents death and the anger of God to the body, the Devil does not hinder that. He often lets the poor soul run with the body to the "houses of stone" [the churches] or wherever it wants. *He encourages it most willingly of all to go to the stone churches*, and there he says to the soul: "Now you are godly and devout; you go diligently to church."

25. But what does he do then? When anyone teaches about the Temple of Christ and about the *New Birth* <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "New Birth" is the essential spiritual transformation required to enter the Kingdom of Heaven.</note>, then he sows other thoughts into the "spirit of this world" <note>The part of human consciousness tied to earthly life and material concerns.</note> within man. Sometimes he sows *covetousness*; sometimes he sets the eyes upon *pride, status, and beauty*; sometimes he catches the spirit with *lust and imagination* toward men or women (according to their sex) and tickles the heart with wanton lust; sometimes the listeners are lulled fast asleep.

26. But when the preacher is a *sophister* <note>original: "Sophister"; here meaning a deceptive or superficial theologian who uses clever but hollow arguments.</note>, a malicious slanderer, or a ranter—or perhaps many times in the performance of his *office* and with a good intention, he rebukes men according to what they deserve—*there the Devil sets open every door and gate*. He tickles the hearts [of the hearers] with this, and the heart wishes for more and more of *that*, which feels very fine [to keep them from falling asleep].

27. And when such people go from church, they can *repeat every word very easily*, especially those parts that tend toward the disgrace of others. They feast themselves on that all week long; it is more acceptable to them than the Word of God.

28. Behold, this is a Devil in an angelic form: when people suppose that if they just run to church together, such a person *is a very good Christian*. But if they have learned nothing more than to scorn, mock, and deride others, and bring that *home* to their families, it would have been better if they had been wallowing in the mire all that time, or if they had been fast asleep. 40. Therefore, when we want to know what *Man* is, and why there is so great a difference and *variety* among people—so that one does not act as another does, and one differs in form and feature from another—we must set before us the most inward ground of his [incarnation or] becoming human and consider it; then we shall find everything.

<margin>It <note>Refers to the ground of human origin mentioned in the previous paragraph.</note></margin>
41. For when a person is born again <note>original: "Regenerated"</note> in God so that he sees the Light, and begins to search out *his origin*, then the spirit of the soul searches in all the <term>Three Principles</term> <note>Boehme’s cosmological system consisting of the dark fire-world, the light love-world, and the visible material world.</note> to find what he is in each of them. For we know it, and cannot say otherwise than that we—in the image of the spirit and also of the body—have only one single *rule* [or dominion] within us across all Three Principles. However, that dominion exists in three sources [or qualities]. The spirit and the body are driven according to each Principle, and whichever Principle gains the upper hand in a person—so that the person inclines their will toward it—is the one according to which he performs his work. The other [Principles] merely cling to it, not having sufficient power.

<margin>Or, womb.</margin>
42. But when we speak of the Image <note>The "Image of God" in which humanity was created.</note>, we must look at its foundational ground. For we are sown like a seed in a field into the <margin>womb</margin> *Matrix*. Now, consider what precedes that: nothing but a longing will and the desire of a man and woman to copulate. Yet the *fruit* <note>meaning the child or offspring</note> is not always desired, as we see in the example of those who engage in illicit sex, and indeed even within the state of marriage.

<margin>The substantiality <note>In Boehme’s thought, "Substantiality" refers to a kind of spiritual body or divine matter.</note></margin>
43. Now the question is: what is it that provokes [the urge to copulate] in the male and female of all kinds, as well as in humans? Behold, in Eternity, everything existed in one Being—namely, the <term>Tincture</term> <note>The vital, spiritual essence or "spark" that gives life and quality to matter.</note>, which is the center and cause of life, as has been mentioned at length before. Also present was the <margin>Substantiality</margin>, which is generated out of the Tincture. This Substantiality also has all the forms of the center, yet without fire; for it is a sinking down and cannot kindle life within itself. It is corporeal and provides the body, but not the life; for the fire provides the life.

44. And we give you to understand that in copulation, the man possesses the Tincture and the woman the Substantiality—namely, the *Matrix*—which is generated out of the Tincture. Now observe: *in Eternity* they were within one another, and this world stood therein *as a figure*. For the Wisdom <note>Often referred to as Sophia, the personified divine wisdom.</note> had overshadowed the Tincture and received it into itself, just as the body receives the spirit. This could not be brought into a substance visible to the angels unless God moved Eternity, for the angels themselves exist within a substance.

The **Tincture** <note>The "Tincture" is a term used by Boehme to describe the spiritual power or "soul-light" that gives quality, color, and life to matter.</note> became substantial and prevailed, and this **substantiality** became material; yet it was not divided, for that cannot be—it is only one single <margin>p substance.</margin>

90. Thus the Heart is in anguish, tormented <note>original: "vexed"</note> both within and without. It attains this Liberty through its desire, yet it cannot truly be free, for the sharpness of the Fire remains within its desire. # How Man May Find Himself: Chapter 10

2. There is only *one way* you must go if you wish to find the Great Mystery <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*; the hidden foundation of all existence</note>. If you were to search in the Moon <note>original: *Luna*; often representing silver or the external, reflective physical world</note> all your life, it would be entirely in vain. Your desire would remain merely lunar. If you were to perform great and difficult labor and take pains in Mercury <note>representing the volatile spirit or the intellect</note>, assuming the Stone lies there, your *alchemy* would prove to be nothing but dung and dross.

<margin>a Or, upon the Body.</margin>
3. When you arrive at Venus, you may suppose you have the Sun <note>original: *Sol*; representing gold or the divine heart</note> and that it is Gold. 9. Christ says: *“Seek first the Kingdom of God, and all other things will be added to you.”* It all lies in the act of willing, for the will creates the desire, and the desire receives where nothing seems to exist—though indeed, something is there. Yet it is hidden from us humans unless a person has attained the Stone upon the Cross <note>original: *Stone upon the Crosse*; a mystical and alchemical symbol for Christ or the spiritual core of reality</note>. Then they find what Reason says does not exist; for that which has not existed from eternity does not exist at all, and we can know nothing of it. We only know that which is and has always been—though indeed *not revealed to us humans*—but which exists within God in His wisdom from eternity to eternity.

10. Therefore, although we speak of *two* kingdoms—namely <note>original: *viz.*</note>, the Kingdom of God and the kingdom of this world—as if we saw them with *physical* eyes, do not find it strange. If God reveals Himself in a person, then that person is in *two* kingdoms and sees with *twofold* eyes. Yet this path is not as hard or difficult as Reason’s search in outward things; *it all lies in the will*. The outward will must enter into the inward. It must deny itself, as if it were dead to the outward world and had no life in it, and yet it still lives. Just as God lives and exists in the outward world while the outward world is "dead" to Him (meaning it cannot comprehend Him), so also you, O human, exist with your soul in the inward realm. However, your soul’s will has turned itself—along with *Adam*—toward the outward. Therefore, if you wish to behold God and eternity, turn your will back toward the inward; then you are as God Himself. For you were created this way in the beginning. Thus you live according to the inward will toward God and in God, and according to the outward [*will you live*] in this world. You possess both kingdoms as your own and are indeed *rightly* an image and likeness <term>similitude: a likeness or formal correspondence</term> of God. You search out all things and find what lay hidden in secret; for you find that in eternity and behold it reflected back in the "out-birth" <note>original: *Out-birth*; the physical world as an external manifestation or "growth" from the spiritual realm</note> in its physical form <note>original: *Figure*</note>.

11. The foundation of this world’s creation is much easier to know within the *inward person*—through the will of God—than visible things are to the *outward* [person]. The outward person understands less of what he sees with his eyes, touches with his hands, hears with his ears, smells with his nose, and tastes with his mouth than the inward person understands of the *foundation* and existence of the outward realm. The inward person indeed sees the creature in its fundamental essence, yet remains as if dead to the outward world while still living within it. And in living for the outward, he lives for God regarding His works of wonder—revealing and bringing into *being* that which was hidden in the spiritual form.

13. Therefore, desire is now a different thing than the will. The will is *without* substance, while desire creates substance. Thus, out of the Eternal Nothingness has come everything that exists. Before that, there was nothing but a will, which was like a Virgin without an image, yet it contained a blueprint <note>original: *figure*</note> of an image within that will. This blueprint revealed the Spirit and brought it into a state of Being, as we perceive in the form of this world. 14. Therefore, we explain the Creation to you in this way: to "create" means to grasp within the will whatever exists as a blueprint in that will. For when a *carpenter* wants to build a house, he must first frame a *model* of it in his mind <note>original: *willing*</note>, deciding how he will build it; then he builds it according to the model in his will.

That was the Heaven which He created on the *Second Day*. He tested the work on the *Third Day* and allowed forms and images to grow out of the earth from its underlying properties <note>original: *Essences*</note>—specifically trees, herbs, and grass—which were images of the properties of desire. But the Image of the Spirit remained hidden, even though it existed *until the Fourth Day*. (Understand here) that a "day" without the sun is one full rotation of the wheel of Nature within the desire of the will. The Inward Will is governed by the *Number Six* (representing the six spirits of nature), and the outward will in the desire of the blueprint also has the *Number Six*, mirroring the Spirit. These *two kingdoms*—the inward and the outward—combine their "sixes" to make twenty-four <note>original: $^m$foure and twenty</note>. These divide themselves into four parts: six before noon, and six after noon, six before midnight, and six after midnight, until the beginning of morning again.

18. Therefore, we tell you that those to whom the *Number Ten* is revealed also have it placed in their will to speak no more than what is required and necessary for the world, at the proper time as need requires and as is known in God.

In this Creation, the *Third Kingdom*—namely <note>original: *viz.*</note>, the Kingdom of Anger—pressed hard in with it; and there went forth all manner of *beasts*, *birds*, *fish*, *worms*, and whatever moves and lives. All went forth out of the outward Matrix and stood upon the Earth. In the Deep <note>Boehme's term for the expanse of space</note> went forth all sorts of spirits of fire (such as the *Ascendents* and the *Phoenix*), and in the air also all sorts of spirits, according to the substance of the air; and in the water and in the earth, all sorts of spirits, each one according to the property of its ^r *Mother*. The whole Deep between the stars <note>original: *Constellations*</note>, as far as the Word gave itself into the Creation, is nothing but a life and stirring of spirits.

21. Now Reason asks: since the Devil dwells in this world and has his princely domain there, whereabouts does he dwell then? Behold, Oh Man, consider this well. There are in the whole Deep no more than seven ^s *orbits* <note>original: *Revolutions*</note>, which roll and turn about like a wheel, or as the Life winds itself about the soul. The *Heart*, as the Center, stands still in the midst: that is, the ^t *Sun*. The ^t *orbits* about the Sun are the six *planets*, acting as Spirits of the Center, and the *seventh orbit is the Earth*, which turns itself *once about in twenty-four hours*, and runs along in the course of the *planets* once a year. Besides this, it carries the *Moon* with it about the *Sun*, as the others do also, but some in shorter and some in much longer time. For example, first ^u *Saturn* in twenty-nine years, because of his large course; but the ^x *Moon*, which runs back, does it every month, twelve times in a year, and passes ^y slightly further [in a *thirteenth revolution*].

22. Now *all of this together* makes the wheel of the birth, within which stands the *Word Fiat* <note>original: *Verbum Fiat*; "The Word: Let it be done"</note>, which has driven the *Devil* out from this circle. Thus, he dwells outside this circle, and there is a great darkness about the *crown of stars* in the firmament, so that many stars in the firmament are not seen because of the darkness. This otherwise has a great significance for Men, which we would indeed mention if the world were not so mad and did not allow the *Devil* to drive it—who mocks all manner of *revelations* so that he may blindfold Men. In the Last Time, it shall stand manifest to the Children who see with *both eyes* [namely, with the *eye that sees into eternity* and the *eye that sees into that which is temporary*].

<margin>a Having eyes within and without.</margin>
24. *This* cannot be described by a circle, for the sun stands innermost in the most inward circle, and the other planets are always further outward, reaching even to the Crown which includes the outermost heaven. It cannot be understood by outward reason, but the Spirit understands it within itself; for as *the Spirit is, so is this circle also*. Consider the Three Principles: the outermost is also the innermost—something the outward spirit of our reason cannot conceive, for *it is* only *one* and not *three* in number. 25. Although the wise *Magi* <note>original: *Magi*; ancient astronomers or wise men</note> and mathematicians have made a sphere and described the wheel, that is not enough. It is indeed a help to the unskilled to consider the *Mysterium Magnum* <note>Latin: "Great Mystery"; the hidden source or spiritual foundation of the universe</note>, the Great Mystery. But the wheel has a much more subtle understanding and cannot be made into any circle in this manner. For it goes into itself toward the heart of the *Sun*, and out from itself toward the *figure* of substantiality <note>the physical or tangible manifestation of spiritual essence</note>. It drives upward and downward, for the Spirit of the Tincture <note>a term for the transformative life-force or spiritual essence</note>—namely, the true fire-life—drives *upward* and inward toward the liberty of God. Yet it desires the Spirit of Substantiality, which drives *downward*, for without that, the fire-life cannot survive. Thus, the fire-spirit turns itself around, as if *sideways*, and always reaches after the spirit of substantiality, while the spirit of substantiality flies from the fire. But since it is generated out of the fire-life and cannot be severed from it, it is *wheeled around* with the fire-spirit. When the fire-spirit wheels to the right side and reaches after the spirit of substantiality, then the spirit of substantiality also wheels on the left side upward. This creates a circular motion, with one chasing the other. For substantiality flies from the fire, and yet it comes out of the fire—just as you see that air comes out of fire, and <margin>b</margin> out of the air comes water, which is the substantiality.

31. Therefore, let the reader be warned not to dive further into these very deep writings, nor plunge his will deeper than what he understands <note>original: "apprehendeth."</note>. This life goes inward even to the *Thousandth Number* and searches into the *Deep of the Deity* with all its *wonders*. He leads your will, when it is submitted to Him, into the *Virgin of His Wisdom* so that you may behold all *wonders*. Mark this: *every imagination* creates *substantiality*, and that is where you stand. You must go out from that again, or else you shall not see God.

32. Therefore *Christ* teaches us *humility*, *love*, *purity of heart*, and to be *merciful*. He calls upon us to seek the will of God and to submit ourselves to it. For in *God's* will, we are able to do *ALL* things; our own nature must not do it, but God Himself...

Every living thing was in awe of you. You had your own food from the Paradisaical fruit to sustain the outward life, and the *Word of the Lord* <note>original: "Verbum Domini"</note> to sustain the inward life of the soul. You would have lived eternally without sorrow or the feeling of any sickness or disease, in pure joy and delight, and moreover, without care or toil. Your mind was like the mind of a child playing with his father's wonders [or craftsmanship]. *No knowledge* of any evil will was in you; no greed, no pride, no envy, no anger, but all was a play of Love.

They sigh, turn, and move toward abstinence or amendment. That is a strong combat of the soul against the spirit of this world. For the soul often does a thing that it never had in its mind or heart, much less intended to do, yet it is suddenly entangled and overcome.

40. For God is nothing but *goodness* and does not will evil. He warns man beforehand that he should still the wrath by turning back and departing from that anger. But when this is not done, He allows that to come which man has awakened—namely wars, famine, and pestilence. Now, God does not do this, but man himself, who makes wars. Then heaven withdraws its fruitfulness, and the spirit of this world kindles itself in the hellish poison and wrath; thus diseases and the plague <note>original: "Pestilence"</note> come forth, for which God is not to blame. Rather, *man* has awakened them, and they devour him; for by this, the anger is sharpened and acquires a longing to devour. For men awaken it in their wickedness and malice, and kindle it, whereas otherwise it would be at rest.

41. You must understand it this way: *Adam* has left this to us as an inheritance. If he had continued in the will of God, the anger would *not have touched him* throughout eternity, and the devil would have been shut up in the wrath. Therefore, the devil has wrestled with man and thrown him into sin, so that man has awakened the anger in the spirit of this world, in which the devil is the *Great Prince*. He increases his kingdom with the souls of men, and thus *the devil is a prince of this world*. Otherwise, he could not touch a fly or move a leaf if man had not kindled the property <gloss>[and working]</gloss> of the anger. He has great access and power over such a spirit.

...evil is; for we demonstrate it to you this way: there are *two sorts of* dominions <note>original: "Dominions"; these are realms of influence or governing powers within the person</note> in man, even while he lies as a seed enclosed in the mother's womb. These exist as *two tinctures* <note>original: "Tinctures"; in this context, spiritual qualities or life-forces that define a being's nature</note>: one from the eternal matrix <note>original: "Matrix"; the spiritual womb or generative source</note>, which is the *tincture* of the soul, and the other from the center of this world, which comes from the spirit and life of this world. He speaks sweet words with his mouth, but the spirit of his heart is *poison*, and he *thinks only of how to do evil or mischief*, using a pretense of fair behavior to hide it. Such a person dwells in *two kingdoms, namely* in this world and with the devil. He does not believe in any God at all, for he considers himself a god. Thus the devil tickles his heart so that he supposes the kingdom of God consists of *historical knowledge*. He thinks that if he can say there is one God in three persons, and that God became man and has turned his grace and favor toward us, then he is a Christian and [sufficiently] a child of God.

He is just like the hypocrite who clings to the *history* and considers the knowledge [of those facts] to be *faith*. No, sir: righteousness and truth must follow faith. Even though the devil assaults man through his outward spirit (*which may be evil due to its constellation*) and often *overthrows* him, the heart suddenly desires righteousness and truth again and is at odds with the devil concerning the sin committed.

44. But a false, wicked soul does not care for righteousness; if it can only cover its sin, then it is satisfied. It seeks merely to deceive under an outward appearance, which it carries around in the hypocritical spirit of this world. Its *holiness* is a mere outward show, and it does not know the will of God at all. Instead, it supposes the will of God consists of *ceremonies*. But ceremonies are <margin>i Or, in.</margin> ^i of this world and are only signs so that the simple laity <term>The "laity" refers to the common people who are not members of the clergy.</term> might consider what God has to do with man.

For it must be as pure as it was when it was created upon the Cross; it must be regenerated upon the Cross of Christ and enter with Christ into the flesh and blood of Christ, through the death of Christ, through the anger of God, into the *Ninth Number* <note>In the author's mystical system, the "Ninth Number" represents the spiritual realm or the "tincture" that precedes the full presence of the Trinity</note> as into the **tincture** <term>tincture: a spiritual essence or transforming power that infuses matter with divine quality</term> of the eternal divine Fire. There it stands as a creature before the *Tenth Number* <note>The "Tenth Number" represents the Holy Trinity and the ultimate presence of God</note>, as before the Holy Number Three, and humbles itself before the Number Three. Then the Majesty of the Number Three embraces it as a dear child. So, humility is the food and strength of the Majesty, out of which the *Brightness* goes forth from eternity to eternity.

51. Where will you, hypocrite, remain with your glistening luster, which is generated out of covetousness and pride? Oh you children of God, *go out from this Whore* <note>A common Reformation-era reference to the "Whore of Babylon," symbolizing a corrupt or false church</note>; she stands on the Devil’s stage and is carried in a show of triumph, to God’s disgrace and contempt.

52. Listen and see, you poor soul; we will show you the very *Antichrist* who dominates over the whole world, whom God has made known to us so that you might see him. For you have until now accounted him a god, but now his shame must come to light. For he is so secret that none know him unless they be born of God, so that they understand God’s essence and will; otherwise, he remains hidden in every man. For there is no one who does not have him and carry him in *his heart*. Even if one is a child of God, yet does not have the deep knowledge of God, he still **clings** to him; for the Devil has insinuated himself into him in the form of an angel. Therefore, mark what follows here, for it is *the Number of the Seventh Seal* and **declares** the Eternal Day.

53. Observe it, you children of God: For I myself formerly, before the time of my high knowledge, did thus reverence and honor him and supposed it was according to God’s will. For I was taught no otherwise, and the whole world is in the same mindset; though that does not hurt the ignorant person (for he may be saved in his simplicity well enough), yet God will *reveal him in this last time.*

54. Behold! You poor, wounded soul, you stand and pray like this: *“O God, forgive me my sins, let your anger cease, and receive me into your Grace.”* This is very well done, but you do not understand how God receives a poor sinner. You suppose it is like when you come before the prince or judge of the land after you have forfeited your life; you pray to him, and he <sup>p</sup> pardons your misdeed out of grace, and so you are acquitted and freed. But your sins fly in your face, and your heart accuses you, saying you are still guilty of the punishment. And this is exactly how you also come before God, and so many hypocrites are produced this way. You suppose God, in His essence and Spirit, takes your sins away from you. Do you not know what the Scripture says: that *all our works shall follow us*? And if it happened as you imagine, then God would have to move Himself according to every person's will and purpose when they call upon Him to cast their sins away. Yet, from eternity, God has moved Himself *no more than twice*: once with the creation of the world and all creatures, and a second time in Christ’s <sup>q</sup> becoming man, where the Heart of God moved itself. 

[Note: The *third time* God will move Himself in the power of the Holy Spirit through the mouth of Christ at the *Last Judgment Day*, when all shall return again into the ether <note>original: "Ether," here referring to the spiritual atmosphere or the primordial state of existence</note>. The *first* moving is according to the Father; the *second* according to the Son; and the *third* according to the Holy Spirit. Otherwise, He moves Himself *no more in eternity*.]

<margin>r That is, the Fire of Wrath.</margin>

55. Behold! When God forgives your sins when you call upon Him, He takes nothing away from you, nor does He fly down from heaven into you. For He is *from eternity in your soul*, but in His own "principle" <term>principle: a distinct realm of existence or spiritual state</term>. As far as He is concerned, your soul has only gone out from His principle—understand this as going out from the Holy Will in the "Majesty" <note>The "Majesty" refers to the glorious, light-filled aspect of God's presence</note> and into the "Anger" <note>The "Anger" refers to the dark, consuming fire of God's judgment or the harsh root of existence</note>. Now, in the Anger, you were in eternal death. But the man Christ, who is God and man, has made a passage through death and anger to the Majesty of God. You only need to turn and go through that passage—through the death of Christ and through the Anger—into the Majesty. There, you will be embraced like the most beloved angel who never committed any sin. Also, no sin will be known in you, only God’s "deeds of wonder," which must be revealed in the Anger. For Love has nothing to do with that fire [ *that is, Love cannot reveal the wonders of the Anger* ], nor does it mix itself with the <sup>r</sup> fire, but flies from it.

56. Now, therefore, when you pray like this: *O God! Forgive me,* you always doubt whether God will hear you and come into your heart because of your sins. Behold! Do not doubt; for by your doubting, you despise and show contempt for His Majesty. This doubting is also a sin. Instead, throw all your sins together into one heap and come f earnestly with your desiring soul, in humility, to God, and enter into Him. Do nothing but *turn* your soul out from the will of this world and into the will of God. Cast yourself, with your whole reason and all your thoughts, into the will of God; and although your heart and the Devil say an absolute "No," make your outward reason dead. Enter in with force and continue steadfastly. Do not look back, as *Lot’s* wife did, *who was turned back into sulfur and into a pillar of salt* <note>Genesis 19:26. In this context, it refers to the danger of looking back at one's old worldly life or sins with longing or doubt.</note>; but stand fast. Let the Devil, the spirit of this world, and even your own heart with its flesh and blood struggle however they want—give no place to reason. When reason says, *“you are without God,”* then say, "No, *I am in God; I am in Heaven in Him; I will not depart from Him for all eternity.*" The Devil may keep my sins, and the world may keep this body, yet I live in the will of God. His life shall also be my life, and His will shall be my will. I will be dead to my own reason, so that HE may live in me; all my doing shall be His doing. Give yourself up to Him in all your purposes. Whatever you take in hand, commit it to His pleasure and government, so that all may be done t in His will. Behold! If you do this, all evil lusts will depart from you; for you stand fast in the presence of God, and the Virgin of His Wisdom <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, personified in mystical tradition as the soul's guide and heavenly bride.</note> leads you and u reveals to you the way to eternal life. She warns you of evil or false ways, and she always drives you toward abstinence, amendment, and submission or resignation.

57. The reason you have such great obstacles and hindrances of doubting in this way is caused by the struggle of the soul against the Devil, who lays himself in the path like a filthy pig. Therefore, throw your sins upon his neck and do not doubt. If you cannot stop that doubting, then reach out with your soul into God, *for God is in you.* Christ has opened the gates to His Father; simply enter in, and let nothing keep you back. Even if Heaven and Earth and all creatures should say you cannot, do not believe them. Go forward, and you will suddenly get in. As soon as you come in, you will receive a *new body* for the soul—that is the body of Christ, who is God and man—and you will afterwards have ease and refreshment in your heart. You will find one who will draw you, set the falsehood of the world before your eyes, and warn you about it.

59. Or are we the only ones who say this? Does Christ not say: *“When the unclean spirit leaves a man, he walks through dry places seeking rest and finding none. Then he returns to his house, and when he arrives, he finds it swept and decorated. You have driven out Satan, cleansed your heart, and have well swept and decorated your house of sin. And now, when you are secure and careless, the Devil comes with all the *seven forms of nature* <note>In Böhme’s theology, these are the seven foundational properties or "source-spirits" of all reality. He thrusts the old worldly lusts back into your heart, from which all wickedness and blasphemies are born. Then he binds the poor soul fast to sin and prevents it from pursuing abstinence or improvement, but instead leads it into fleshly lusts. When the soul begins to struggle, he says, "Tomorrow, tomorrow," until he catches the prey <note>original: "Venison." Here used metaphorically for the soul as hunted game.</note>.

60. He has *no rest* in Hell, but in the soul of man he finds joy and pleasure. There he can reveal his malicious wonders, amusing himself even after this life ends, for Hell and the anger of God desire that.

62. Now I would gladly know how the sins of the repentant sinner—who casts himself into God’s will and who goes forth from the reasoning of this world into God’s mercy—can have his sins retained <note>original: "retained"; held against him or kept in place.</note>. And much more would I gladly know how one sinful man can bring another out of Hell and into the Kingdom of Heaven when he cannot even get in himself, and only goes about trying to make the Devil proud with his covetousness by selling the forgiveness of sins for money? On the contrary, all sins are drowned only in Christ’s new body, in Christ’s flesh and blood. As Isaiah says in the person of Christ:
> *I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the people there was none with me; I alone blot out your sins, and none besides me.* <note>Isaiah 63:3 and 43:25.</note>
But if what the Antichrist <note>A common Reformation-era term for the institutional church or any authority seen as usurping Christ's role.</note> boasts of were true, then one devil must drive away another. If that were so, what would become of the new regeneration in Christ’s flesh and blood, by which our souls are brought into God?

63. If it had been possible for God to take away Adam’s sin in such a [legalistic] manner, God would not have needed to become human to bring us into God again. He might instead have simply forgiven Adam his sin, just as a prince pardons a murderer and grants him his life. No, sir: *you yourself* must depart from sin and enter into the will of God. For God does not stand by like an earthly king and forgive sins with mere words. It must be a power; you must go out from the fire and into the light. For God is not a statue or an image for us to stand before and give "good words" to; rather, *He is a Spirit, and He penetrates through the heart and the innermost thoughts* <note>original: "reines"; literally "kidneys," historically considered the seat of deep emotion and intent.</note>. He is the Fire of Love, and His "center of nature" is the Fire of Anger. Even if you were in Hell among all the devils, you would still be "in God," for the Anger is also *His; it is His Abyss*. Therefore, when you go out from that anger, you go into the Love of God—into the liberty that is without distress or pain.

64. There is no other forgiveness to be understood except that you go out from the will of this world, from your flesh, and from the Devil’s will, and enter into God’s will. Then God’s will receives you, and so you are freed from all sins. For the sins remain in the "Fire" [of Anger], but your will remains in the Tincture of God <note>A Böhmean term referring to the spiritual essence or "infusion" of divine light and life.</note>, which the Divine Majesty enlightens. Everything is near you: your sins are near you, but they *do not touch you*. For as we have mentioned to you before, the Still Eternity is a state of liberty. Yet do not think that this eternity will take your sins—your abominations and wickedness—into itself. Those belong to the Anger of God; there they must stay and be given to the Devil. But they stand beneath you in the "center," and you are like a beautiful sprout and fruit which springs up through the Anger toward the Love and toward God’s deeds of wonder. And yet, the Anger is not "in" God [proper], but in the *Abyss*. When the Devil raised himself above God, then he

65. The text in Matthew, chapter 16, verses 18–19, has another meaning in it: *The Temple of Christ (that is, Christ’s children) is Christ’s Bride. He has adorned her with his fairest ornament; and just as he has loved us and brought us through himself into God his Father, so we should love one another. In the place of God, we should make known to him the forgiveness of his sins, lay our hands upon him, and make him a partaker of our body and congregation; and so our spirit and virtue (or power) will rest upon him, as was seen with the Apostles of Christ.*

<margin>* Earnest desire.</margin>

66. And when we receive him into the congregation of Christ, then he [becomes] our brother. When we say, "your sins are forgiven," then they are drowned in the blood and death of Christ, and he is a member of us. We do not take away his sins from him, but *Christ in us drowns them in his blood through our and his faith.* When we lay our hands upon him and pray over him, then we—with our will which is [given up] into God—penetrate into his will. We bring him into our will, as into one [and the same] body in Christ, to the Father. His will becomes our will, for he gives himself up through Christ into the Bride <note>The "Bride" refers to the spiritual community of true believers united with Christ.</note> as into our will, *which is also God’s will.* We receive him with good cause into our love, into our will, and sink ourselves down in him through Christ into God. *Thus we forgive him his sins*, for we are the congregation and Bride of Christ, whom he loves. What we do, Christ does in us, and God does in Christ. It is all one: Christ is ours, and God is Christ’s; and the converted sinner is ours, and Christ’s, and also God’s. We live in one body, have one Spirit, and are one flesh. As we enter into the will of God, so we also *take our brother along with us.* We cast the sins away behind us into the fire of anger, but we live and flourish in God. *We have the key of Heaven and of Hell.* When we make known to a sinner his sins and he will not be converted, then *we bind him up in the abyss*; for we pass through and shut it up, and then he must swelter in his sins. Then the Devil buffets him; when we no longer draw him with our word (which has power), then the Devil draws him. But if he turns at length, then we have power to take him away from the Devil again and—through our Spirit in Christ—to bring him into God.

### The Highly Precious Gate

68. Now Reason asks: How can Christ’s body be our body? Is he a creature? How can we dwell in the body of Christ?

69. Behold, O Man: *Adam* was our father and also our mother. Now we all possess *Adam’s* flesh, soul, and spirit, for we are all begotten from one and the same flesh, soul, and spirit. We are all members of him (as the branches are members of the tree), and he brought us into death.

<margin>z Or, into.</margin>
70. He had the fair Virgin of the Wisdom of God within him, who is *everywhere* and is the fullness of all things, just as God himself is. He lost this; he should have left it to us as an inheritance, but he departed from it. However, the *second Adam*, *Christ*, came forth from God and was the Heart of God, and he had the fair Virgin within him. He took our flesh and soul into his Virgin, and that became flesh, soul, and spirit: flesh of our flesh, and soul of our soul, yet he remained God. Our flesh stood in *Christ* in the *Holy Ternary* <note>original: "Ternario Sancto"</note>; he received from us <margin>z</margin> into the Virgin of God both the eternal and also the earthly flesh—though indeed it was only the earthly source [and property], for nothing that is corruptible enters into God.

<margin>a Became or was made.</margin>
<margin>b Or, the matter is about the Eternal Will.</margin>
71. When the *Word* <margin>a</margin> entered the flesh, it then became heavenly, just as in *Adam* it had become earthly. For the flesh of *Christ* was brought into the Word within the Eternal Will, so that the flesh and the Word were *one undivided person*. Now <margin>b</margin> this work is accomplished in the Eternal Will, from which *Adam* had strayed, and God brought us back into that will through the soul of *Christ*.

72. Now *Christ’s* soul is our soul, for it is *Adam’s* soul; and *Christ’s* flesh is our flesh, for he took it upon himself from our humanity. And the fair Virgin of God in *Christ* is our Virgin, for *Christ* has placed her into our souls. So now, if we give ourselves up entirely to *Christ*, then *Christ* lives in us and we in him. Although the outward mortal body still clings to us, yet *Christ* lives in us, and at the end of the world, he will present us—wholly pure and without blemish—in his flesh.

### Of the True Knowledge of What Man Is. Chapter 11.

73. Thus we are *one body* in him: for *he* is our body in God, and Adam is our body in this world. There is no such gross or unrefined <note>original: "untoward"</note> body in God, but rather a body in power, with heavenly flesh and blood. Where our will is, there our heart is also; God is in us. And when we enter into his Will, then we put his wisdom onto ourselves, and in that wisdom, *Christ is a Man*. Thus we enter into his humanity and are a *New Man* in the life of Christ, in the soul of Christ, in Christ’s flesh, in the spiritual essence <note>original: "Tincture"</note> of Christ, and in the majesty of Christ. And Christ is in his Father, and his Father is the *Eternity* and the *fulfillment* <note>original: "End"</note> of nature.

74. And where will you go further than this, you poor man? Do not let the Devil and the Antichrist fool you. *No man* has any power in God unless he is in the Will of God—in God’s love in Christ—and then he possesses the soul and flesh of Christ. But if he has that, then he is not a greedy wretch, nor a flattering hypocrite who sells the Kingdom of Heaven for money, as *Simon Magus offered to give money to Saint Peter, asking him to give him the power so that on whomever he laid hands, they would receive the Holy Spirit. Then Peter said: "May you be cursed along with your money! Do you suppose that the gifts of God can be sold for money?"*

75. And where, then, do you get your power and authority, you deceptive reasoners <note>original: "Sophisters"; here referring to those who rely on academic logic rather than spiritual experience</note>, to sell the Kingdom of Heaven and seize it for your own power? You are not Christ’s disciples, but the disciples of the Antichrist, the Whore of Babylon <note>original: "Babell"</note>. *No priest* is capable of the office unless he is in the will of God; his absolution <note>original: "Absolution"; the formal release from guilt or sin</note> is no absolution. Instead, it is the congregation of Christ, to whom the sinner gives himself up, that absolves him. The *false teacher* <note>original: "Sophister"</note> is as useful to the Church as a fifth wheel is to a wagon.

76. You false teacher, how will you impart the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note> which you do not possess? The congregation or church has it, and the repentant sinner who comes to you has it, but you are a deceptive reasoner and are more fit to be in a stable of oxen than in the church. How can the Devil absolve a sorrowful sinner? And you only serve your <margin>c belly-god <note>original: "Belly-God"; an idol of one's own physical appetites or greed</note>.</margin> idol, the belly.

77. O you blind world, how are you blinded! You suppose you should not dare to meddle with the <margin>d The *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>, the office of the ministry.</margin> *Great Mystery*, and that you are not worthy of it, and that the <margin>e Those who call themselves theologians <note>original: "Divines"</note> and ministers.</margin> *priest* alone is worthy of it. But the covenant belongs to the believers, and not to the deceptive reasoners. # Chapter 11: Of the True Knowledge of What Man Is.

108. There are Three Principles (or *Three Kingdoms*); two are eternal, and one has a beginning and is temporary. Each of them desires Man, for Man is an image of *all three*. The Being of all beings is a longing, seeking, and desiring that arises from the Eternal Will, and that Will is *Eternity*.

<margin>Government.</margin>
109. In God there is no rule or control, except within the Three Principles and their creatures. In God, there is nothing but one single *Spirit*, which comes to support His whole Being in the water and in the fire, out of which everything exists. He is not a destroyer, but a preserver of things. If anything perishes, the fault lies in the *rule of Nature* <note>Böhme refers to the "Dominion of Nature" as the complex interplay of natural forces that can lead to decay</note>. However, that which comes from the Eternal cannot perish; it only changes into another quality <note>original: "property"</note>. For this <insert>[reason]</insert> we give you warning: all the teaching and seeking in this world is only so that you may be warned of the harsh source or quality of the Fire. There is indeed *a life* in it, and no creature can survive without having that life; but we who are human were not created for that life. Therefore, God would have every creature remain in that quality in which He created it, so that His Eternal Will may stand firm and not be broken.

<margin>Humanity.</margin>
110. Everything has *Free Will*, and within that, its own tendency toward its nature. The entire existence of this world, the angelic world, and even the hellish world is simply *a marvel* in the presence of God. He has set light and darkness before everyone; you may embrace whichever you wish. You will not change God’s essential Being by your choice. His Spirit goes out from Him and meets all those who seek Him. It is God’s own seeking, in which God desires humanity, for humans are His image. He created us according to His *whole Being*, in which He wishes to see and know Himself. Indeed, He dwells in Man—why then are we searching for Him for so long? Let us simply *seek to know ourselves*, and when we find ourselves, we find *everything*. We do not need to run anywhere to seek God, for we cannot serve Him that way. If we simply seek and love one another, then we love God. What we do to one another, we do to God. Whoever seeks and finds his brother or sister has sought and found God. In Him, we are *all one* body of many members, each having its own office, role <note>original: "Government"</note>, and work; and that is the marvel of God.

111. Before the time of this world, we were known in His Wisdom, and He created us into existence so that there might be a delight <note>original: "sport"; this refers to the "Divine Play" or the interaction between God and His creation</note> in Him. *Children* are our teachers (in all our intelligence and cunning, we are but fools compared to them). When they are born, their first lesson is to learn to play by themselves, and when they grow larger, *they play with one another*. In this way, God from eternity (in His Wisdom, in our hidden childhood) has *played with us*. But when He created us in...

112. Dear children, what do we mean, that we are so obedient to the Devil? Why do we contend so much about a tabernacle <note>A "tabernacle" here refers to a temporary dwelling, signifying either the physical body or earthly institutions</note> *which we have not made*? No, this country is not ours, nor is this government ours; it is our *Mother's* <note>Böhme often refers to "the Mother" as Divine Wisdom (Sophia) or the eternal nature of God</note>, and the Devil has defiled it. Here we contend about a garment because one brother has a fairer garment than another; and yet the *Mother* puts everyone’s own garment upon them. Why, therefore, do we contend with our Mother, who has brought us forth? Are we not all her children? 113. We go into the garden of roses, and there are lilies and flowers enough; we will make a garland for our sister, and then she will rejoice with us. We have a round <note>original: "Round"; a traditional circle dance</note> to dance, and we will all hold hands together. Let us be very joyful; there is no more power to hurt us, for our Mother takes care of us. We will go under the fig tree—how abundant is its fruit! How fair are the pine trees in *Lebanon*! Let us be glad and rejoice so that our Mother may have joy because of us.

114. We will sing a song of the driver [or oppressor] who has set us at variance: How is he *captured*? Where is his power? He is not to be found here; neither has he gained the defiled garment which we contended about, for the Mother has it in her keeping. How poor he is! He dominated over us, but now he is bound. O Great Power, how you are thus brought to scorn; you that flew aloft *above the cedars* are now laid underfoot and are so void of power. *Rejoice you heavens, and you children of God, for he who was our driver [oppressor and persecutor] who plagued us day and night, is captured; rejoice you angels of God, for humanity is delivered, and malice and wickedness are taken captive.*

<margin>a Or, the business he undertakes. What he gets or acquires.</margin>
<margin>* Or, Initial <note>original: "Inceptive"; meaning something that has a beginning, as opposed to that which is eternal.</note>.</margin>
1. There is nothing more necessary and profitable to a person in the valley of misery upon Earth than to learn to know what he is, from where he comes, and where he is heading. It is vital to know what ᵃ course he takes, and where he goes when he dies. There is nothing more profitable than to know these things. For outward conduct remains in this world, but what the heart conceives, that a person takes with him. The will of the spirit of the soul is eternal. That which is contained within the will of the spirit of the soul—that is what the soul carries with it when the soul and body part. Therefore, it is necessary for us to labor for something that is good, in which the soul may accomplish its eternal activity <note>original: "sport"; Böhme uses this term to describe the joyful, creative play or expression of the spirit</note> and have its joy. For the works of our soul follow after us, while the works of our hands and of the outward spirit remain in this world. Because the soul is in eternity, whatever it creates and imagines here always stands before it—unless the soul breaks that image again. If it is broken, it becomes like a discarded work which the soul has nothing more to do with, for it has moved on from it. The eternal spirit carves an eternal model, and the corruptible and * initial spirit carves a corruptible model. After this time, everything will stand in its own model; for that which the Eternal Will conceives takes on an incorruptible form, unless the Will itself destroys it.

<margin>b Useless.</margin>
2. Therefore, it is good for a person to choose in this life that which is best, in which he may have joy eternally. The finery of this world despises the lowly and simple; riches wring the sweat from the poor (or "grind the faces of the poor"), and great power and authority press and oppress the low and miserable. Great honor despises the simple and will not descend to the level of the needy. Seeing, therefore, that in the other life, the souls of many who have been simple,

...great honor and reverence to men, even from a good intention born of your love, as thankful people toward the government of the *Holy Spirit*. But because you have given such honor to men as belongs only to God (though God was content as long as they continued in the love of God in humility), they have therefore fallen away from ^n what they were into a lust after worldly honor. They have fallen into a desire to dominate your goods and souls with cunning and deceit, and they have become a snare to you. For the Antichristian Devil has slipped into them, and the *Spirit of God* has departed from them. They no longer speak from the Spirit of God, but from their own pride and academic skill. Strange languages <note>original: "strange Languages"; referring to the use of Latin, Greek, and Hebrew by scholars to gatekeep spiritual knowledge from the common people</note> must do the work and must be the ones to bring forth the Great Mystery <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*</note>.

<margin>o Usurped.</margin>
19. But behold, dear brothers, how very thievishly they have dealt with you! They have set themselves up over the Earth and have ^o drawn to themselves all power, might, and honor. They ascribe all authority to themselves and have blinded you with flattering hypocrisy. They have led you away from God into "opinions" <note>denominational sects or private interpretations</note>, and there you go astray. They have egged you on to contention and wars, so that you have murdered one another and wasted your native countries. They have robbed you of body and soul, and also of your goods and wits, and made you believe *you did God good service in it* when you became enemies to those who are not of your opinion; and yet you are all equally blind on both sides.

<margin>p Those who have the "cure of souls"; ministers who receive a "living" (guaranteed income from church lands).</margin>
<margin>q The various ranks of the church hierarchy, such as the ordinations of Deacons, Priests (Presbyters), Bishops, Primates, Archbishops, Cardinals, etc.</margin>
20. Behold! These are the ^p curators over your souls, your spiritual leadership, the clergy. Look upon *Popery* <note>The Roman Catholic system</note>: where has that sprung from? It came from the Devil at *Rome*. He has caused *Asia, Africa, Assyria, Persia*, and *Greece* to depart from his deceit; for the Antichristian "priest-devil" has blinded the whole world and brought them into vain traditions and opinions, turning them away from that unanimous love. He has placed more holiness in one order or opinion than in another and has sold the highest degree of ^q religious orders for money. That order which possessed large and rich estates and revenues had to give much to the *Chief Devil* <note>referring to the Pope or the head of the corrupt system</note> so that he might be fat and a lord upon Earth. The simple laypeople <note>the common people, as opposed to the clergy</note> were persuaded these orders were holiness itself, and so they worshipped before the Dragon in the Book of Revelation and sought pardon, absolution, and the forgiveness of sins from that source. Oh, how the common people were tied to them! Whosoever spoke against it was accounted a *heretic*, and the people burned them with fire. This is what the simple people did, persuaded that they did God good service in doing so.

<margin>r Devotion.</margin>
21. Oh, you simple ^r holiness! You are not guilty in so doing, neither—
