Neither shall it be held against you or accounted to your debt at the Last Day (for you proceeded blindly in it, even though on that day the Holy Martyrs shall be set before your eyes). You have been zealous for God in your blindness. The Blessed Martyrs (who have seen the Light of God) will not, therefore, cast you out of their <margin>t Communion and fellowship.</margin> congregation, seeing that you did not know what you were doing but were blindly led to do it.

22. Yet behold and observe what a zealous will, or an earnest desire, can do if one enters into the will of God with their whole heart. Even if a person does not know what they are doing and is <term>zealous in a strange opinion</term><note>The author refers to being passionate about an unorthodox or incorrect religious doctrine.</note>, if their heart is directed toward God and they believe steadfastly in their ignorance that it is pleasing to God, miracles can happen. Within such an opinion, many great <margin>* Or, Miracles.</margin> wonders and works have been performed in the midst of the Antichristian kingdom; for nothing is impossible for a strong faith.

23. The Antichrist has insinuated himself into these wonders and has created almost as many <margin>e Tenets or Sects and Orders of Religion.</margin> opinions as there are days in the year. Among the believers who have believed so blindly in their particular opinion, even wonders and miracles have been performed. The Antichrist has attributed these to the "opinion" itself, whereas the opinion could not even make a fly move. Rather, it was the firm and strong faith—which moved beyond the opinion toward God—that <margin>u Or, performed the miracles.</margin> awakened those wonders. For the Spirit of God is found in faith, not in opinion, and faith comes from God. When the soul inclines itself toward God while holding an opinion, it lays hold of the Spirit of God. The <term>opinion</term><note>The specific religious dogmas or sects that often divide people.</note> is like the fire; but the soul does not stay in the fire. Instead, it presses out from there into God, blossoming out of the fire like a beautiful flower growing out of the earth.

24. These opinions were tolerable enough to God, and God did not reject them as long as the soul sought God through the opinion, and as long as the Church of Christ <margin>x Or, had a true Government.</margin> maintained a proper governance. But when the Devil crept into it and turned it into a grand, glittering kingdom—when the priests sought only honor, greed, and luxury, and led people away from God toward their own <margin>y The performance of ceremonies.</margin> works—the opinions became completely blind. Because they themselves departed from God into the works of their own hands, following forged and invented paths, God let them go, seeing they would not be directed by His Spirit.

25. And Asia, Africa, and Greece are to be considered fortunate because they have returned from the "works of men" to the one and only God again. Although they have indeed been blind concerning the Kingdom of Christ, their minds continued to focus on the one and only God and remained in harmony with one another; and they have not so...

The *Blessed Martyrs* (who have seen the *Light of God*) will not therefore cast you out of their <margin>t Communion and fellowship.</margin> ^t *Congregation*, seeing you knew not what you did but were blindly led on to do it.

22. Yet *behold* and *observe* what a *zealous will*, or *earnest* desire, can do if one enters into the will of *God* with his whole desire. Although he does not know what he does, and is *zealous* in a strange *opinion* <note>original: "Opinion"; here meaning a specific sectarian doctrine or theological viewpoint</note>, yet his heart is directed toward *God* and *believes* in ignorance very steadfastly that it is pleasing to *God*. In such an *opinion*, many *great* <margin>* Or, Miracles.</margin> * *wonders* and *works* have been done in the midst of the *Antichristian Kingdom*; for there is nothing impossible to a *strong faith*.

23. <margin>e Tenets or sects and orders of religion.</margin> <margin>u Or, performed the miracles.</margin> *Antichrist* has insinuated himself into these *wonders* and has created almost as many ^e *opinions* as there are *days* in the year. Among these, in the *believers* who have so blindly believed in their *opinion*, even *wonders* and *miracles* have been done; and the *Antichrist* has credited the *opinion* for it, whereas the *opinion* could not make a fly stir. Rather, it was the firm and strong *faith*, which reached out from the *opinion* toward *God*, that has ^u awakened the *wonders*. For the *Spirit of God* is in the *faith*, and not in the *opinion*; and the *faith* is from *God*. For the soul inclines itself through the *opinion* toward *God* and lays hold of the *Spirit of God*. The *opinion* is the *fire*; but the soul does not stay in the *fire*, but presses out from there into *God*; it blossoms out of the *fire* like a fair flower [out of the *earth*].

24. <margin>x Or, had a true government.</margin> <margin>y The performance of religious ceremonies.</margin> These *opinions* were *tolerable* enough in *God's* sight, and *God* did not reject them as long as the soul sought *God* through the *opinion*; during that time, the *Church of Christ* ^x stood under a true government. But when the *Devil* crept into it and made a stately, *glittering kingdom* of it—when the *priests* sought only *honor*, *greed* <note>original: "covetousnesse"</note>, and *sensuality* <note>original: "voluptuousnesse"</note> within it, and led people away from *God* merely into their ^y *works*—the *opinions* became altogether blind. For they themselves went out from *God* into the works of their own hands, following forged and invented ways; therefore *God* let them go, seeing they would not be directed by His *Spirit*.

25. And *Asia*, *Africa*, and *Greece* are to be considered fortunate <note>original: "happy"</note> in that they have gone out from the *works of men* and returned to the *one only God* again. Although they have indeed been blind concerning the *Kingdom of Christ*, yet their *mind* continued in the *one only God* and in harmony with one another; and have not so—

27. Behold! Christ says: *Where your treasure is, there your heart is* also. Behold! The soul is *entangled* in the opinion and so runs with it to the *patron* [or author of it] who has taught it so, and seeks him; and if it does not find him, then it becomes sorrowful and has no rest. Thus it hovers between heaven and hell and would gladly <margin>c Or, get away from the Devil.</margin> escape the Devil. *Therefore* it happens that many times poor souls have appeared again in the congregation, or else in houses, fields, and churches, and have cried to the congregation for help *with their prayers*, and have submitted themselves to the [religious] orders, supposing they would find ease. From this, the concept of *Purgatory* was framed. For that soul truly experiences Purgatory if it cannot attain the will of God; and in such fervent casting itself down within its opinion, it has sunk down through that opinion and at length come into the *Still Eternity* <note>In the author's theology, the "Still Eternity" refers to a state of ultimate peace and divine rest beyond the turmoil of nature and human will.</note>. 

But we are referring here to those souls which, within their opinions, have imagined [or sought] after the kingdom of God, and not the souls of the deceivers who have sought their own profit and pleasure therein. Those are completely gone prostituting themselves with the Antichrist, for they are bound to him by an oath. And though they sit in hellfire being unfaithful with him, yet they flatter him with their hypocrisy and reproach God *as if* He had dealt unjustly with them. For whatever the soul does here in this [*lifetime*], in which it involves itself and takes into its will, it carries that with it in its will; and after the death of the body, it cannot be freed from it. For afterwards, it has nothing else but that; and when it goes into that and kindles it, seeking it with diligence, that is merely an unfolding of the same <margin>d Being, essence, or substance of the work it has performed here in this life.</margin> thing, and the poor soul must content itself with *that*. Only during the life of the body can it break off from that thing which it has wrapped up in its will; otherwise, that remains afterward like a broken wheel, which is useless and—

No soul enters into it anymore, nor does it seek anything further within it.

28. Thus we say to you, that after the body is broken, the *Antichristian souls no longer seek the Door of Christ*, for they know nothing of it; they know only what they conceived or accepted here on earth. In that opinion, the souls sink down into the <term>deepest Ground</term> <note>original: "deepest Ground." In the author’s mystical theology, this refers to the "Ungrund" or the foundational abyss of existence where the soul finds its own internal reality.</note>, much deeper than they imagined here. For whatever was known by many people of that same opinion—whatever any or all of them knew within that same belief—that *one soul alone knows*. For it is one body with all those who share the same opinion, and they have one heart in many members, wherein everyone manages their business. This remains so until the Judgment of God, which shall afterwards make a separation; then all the kindreds upon the earth shall howl and lament when they recognize that Judge whom they despised here.

29. Listen, you accursed Antichrist: what answer will you give? You have led the people astray from faith in God and from the justification found in the passion and death of Jesus Christ, leading them instead into your deceitful hypocrisy in opinions, only for the sake of your pride, honor, and greed. You have persuaded them so thoroughly that many of them, in their youth and ignorance, have sworn and vowed to you. What have you done? You have done the same thing Christ said to the Pharisees: *Woe to you, Pharisees, who travel over sea and land until you have made one convert; and when you have made him so, you make him twice as much a child of hell as yourselves* <note>original: paraphrasing Matthew 23:15</note>; and this is also what the Antichrist does.

30. In *Germany*, people suppose they have now escaped from Antichrist through their contentions, but it is not so yet. For those who now curse Antichrist and expose his shame have themselves grown out from the tree of Antichrist; they are the *wolves* and *bears* of Antichrist, who suck from him and devour him. The spirit of this <term>Principle</term> <note>original: "Principle." A technical term in the author's work referring to one of the three fundamental realms of existence: the dark world, the light world, or the external world.</note> has commanded them to do so, and they must do it; for they are one trumpet among the seven angels in the *Book of Revelation*. They all wind one horn and sound it so that the earth shakes; but when the thunder follows, then the *Mystery of the Kingdom of God will be revealed again*, and our Door of Grace in Christ will be opened again—which Antichrist had sealed up—for he shall be thrown down into the abyss. Observe this.

31. They are the children of Antichrist, whom he introduces very finely and subtly. Oh, what a cunning artist the Devil is! If you will not open your eyes, it will continue this way until the end. This is told to the simple, and they are directed to open their eyes, and...

Do not pay attention to opinions; mere heresies reside in opinions. Even if people are zealous in their opinion and press toward God through it—and so attain God and the kingdom of heaven—they still have the tail of Antichrist hanging on them. For they are zealous against others and reproach and persecute *them* who are *not* of their opinion.

32. Mark this, you princes, rulers, and magistrates: do not allow yourselves to be led astray. Keep the teachers within the churches and command them to teach the will of God *in His love*. Do not give them lordly power, and do not put any authority into their hands to create canons and constitutions <note>original: "Cannons and Constitutions." This refers to ecclesiastical laws and dogmatic rules established by church hierarchies.</note>. Otherwise, they will cling to greed, and Antichrist resides in all greed; so, no matter what you do, you will have him *on your neck*.

<margin>Or, learning.</margin>
33. Look to it, you princes, and pay attention to those men who are born of God, and not of *Art* <note>original: "Art." Here, the author means academic training, intellectual scholarship, or "book-learning" devoid of spiritual experience.</note> alone. For wherever there is great <margin>Or, learning.</margin> art without an humble heart inclined toward God—a heart that does not seek its own honor or greed—there is Antichrist most assuredly. For in art resides pride and self-honor, which would gladly rule the world and desire to gain much for themselves. Do not trust these men; they are not *Christ's shepherds*. If you will not follow what is revealed to you, then the last Antichrist will be worse than the first. It will come to such a point that the world will be forced to throw them all headlong into the abyss, as *Daniel* and the *Revelation* show clearly enough, and as we have known it will happen to them. For they are <margin>Or, scourge.</margin> now a broom and <margin>Or, scourge.</margin> rod upon the old Antichrist, their grandfather. But there is *one coming* who will bind them also and set the truth before their faces.

34. Observe it, you children of God: this is a *sign* of the last Antichrist. In his kingdom and opinions, they deny the body and blood of Christ in which we are born in God. Lift up your heads and behold, for your redemption draws near. Do not be led astray and lulled asleep. Do not look with the eyes of others, but open your own eyes and flee from Antichrist into the Spirit of Christ. There is only *one* way to enter into the kingdom of Christ, which is set down as follows:

In obedience to God, yield your will into God's will and do not invent <note>original: "feigne."</note> ways of your own reason, or ask, "Where is *Christ*?" *Direct your path toward Christ and know for certain that Christ is in your heart.* Submit yourself to him in great humility, cast all your purposes and actions into his will and pleasure, and consider that you always stand before the clear face <note>original: "countenance."</note> of God, and that *Christ* sits on the rainbow at the right hand of God *within you*. Consider that you stand *every moment* before the *Holy Trinity* <note>original: "Holy Number Three." This is the author's preferred term for the Triune nature of God.</note>, and that *God the Holy Trinity* always examines and sees the depths <note>original: "Abysse."</note> of your heart. Take care that you do not enter into any deep thought or intellectual searching, but simply into his *love* and <margin>Mercy <note>original German: "Bamhertzigkeit" (Barmherzigkeit).</note></margin> *mercy*. Resolve never to leave it again, but to continue in it forever.

36. And then secondly, consider that you do what is pleasing in the sight of *God the Most High* when you seek out your brothers and sisters in this world with your love—whoever they are, whatever they are called, and whatever *opinion* they hold. Embrace them in your *heart*, pray for them, and help them to wrestle against the *Devil*. As far as is possible, *instruct* them with all humility; but if they will not *receive it*, then put on the garment of *Christ* and be a good example to them. Be serviceable and helpful to them; forgive them when they hurt and wrong you. When they curse you, bless them; when they do you injury—if you cannot turn it to good and avoid them—let it pass, and consider that you are only a *pilgrim* here. Withdraw your *love* from no one, for your *God* in whom you live withdraws himself from no one who simply seeks him. Be ready to yield to your adversary if he ever offers to change his mind. In all your affairs and conversation, love *righteousness*, and always take care that you do your work for *God*. In this world, in this troublesome valley of misery, we must carry out our affairs with labor and effort; we should not retreat into *holes, cloisters, cells, and corners*. For *Christ* says: *Let your light shine before men, so that your Father may be praised for your works.* Do all things from a <margin>sincere heart, from the bottom of your heart.</margin> sincere heart and with a pure mind, and consider that you are doing it for *Christ*, and that the *Spirit of Christ* does it in you. Be always ready, waiting for the *Bridegroom*. Do not allow your *heart* to meditate on or search for any other *opinion*; it is not profitable for you to know much. Let everyone learn to do their own work to provide for their body, whether they are a <margin>Superior <note>original: "Magistrate."</note></margin> *magistrate* or a <margin>Inferior <note>original: "Lay Person."</note></margin> *lay person*.

<margin>Or, respectful</margin> Let the laity <note>original: "Layety" (the common people, as opposed to the clergy).</note> be humble and respectful before the ordinances of God. If any wrong is done to you with an arrogant hand, and it cannot be avoided, consider that you suffer wrong for the sake of the truth, and that this is a great honor for you in Christ in the presence of God.

38. In all your matters, conduct <note>original: "conversation," meaning one's entire way of life and social interaction.</note>, dealings, and actions, always set the judgment of God before your eyes. Take care that you live blamelessly here, for this life is short, and we stand here like a field that is growing. Therefore, see to it that you are good fruit for God, in which all the angels and hosts of heaven may be pleased and rejoice. Bear malice toward no one, for that invites the Devil to take up lodging in you. Be sober and temperate. Do not let the desires of this world persuade you; and though it may happen sometimes, do not persist in it. Go every hour out of death into life. Crucify your own desires through true repentance and conversion from evil.

39. When you are insulted for your fear of God and spoken of evilly—if it is false and untrue—then rejoice most of all that you have become worthy to suffer reproach for the doctrine and honor of Christ. When you are in affliction, do not be dismayed; consider that you are within the will of God. He will suffer no more to be laid upon you than you shall be able to bear.

40. Turn away your eyes from greed, from pride <note>original: "high-mindednesse."</note>, and social status. Do not readily look after such things, so that you are not captivated. *For the Devil catches his birds with status and pride; do not walk into his net.* Be always watchful and never feel too secure, for that bird-catcher <note>original: "fowler."</note> constantly goes about to see where he can catch anyone. Where honest people are mocked and scored, do not go there. Do not make yourselves partakers of such wickedness; do not let it enter into your ears, so that the Devil does not tickle your heart with that foolish laughter and cause you to become infected with it.

41. In summary, entrust yourselves to God in Christ. Pray to God the Father in the name and upon the promise of Christ for his Holy Spirit. Desire it based on Christ's promise, and you will receive it, for he is faithful who has promised it; he will not deny it to you. You will receive it *most certainly*. Only give yourself wholly up to him—that is the greatest and most important thing. Commit everything to his will. When you have the Spirit, he will teach you sufficiently what you are to do. He teaches you how to speak; he gives you a mind, knowledge, and understanding of how to behave yourselves. Do not be anxious about the manner in which you should do a thing when you are dealing with men. Instead, commit all your doings to him; he will perform that in you well enough which is *pleasing to him.*

14. <margin>p The Spirit.</margin>

15. *But Note!* The Godhead had conceived the "Image" in its will—the image which God created in his "Virgin" of Wonders and Wisdom <note>original: "Virgin of his Wonders and Wisdom" — In this context, the "Virgin" refers to Divine Wisdom or Sophia, a heavenly mirror of God's glory, rather than the person of Mary.</note>. God brought together flesh and blood with the "Eternal Tincture" <note>term: Tincture — a spiritual essence or transformative power that gives life and quality to matter.</note> in which the soul lives. This "Eternal Fire" reaches into the Godhead to find the substance of Divine Majesty; it calms, fills, and strengthens itself there. 

This process came out of Mary, through the Virgin, and into the Holy Trinity <note>original: "Ternary"</note>. The Word gave itself to this process as a life within the Tincture of Eternity. It became the spirit, life, and power <note>original: "vertue"</note> of that flesh which grows out of the fire of the soul. For the Spirit was in the Word, and the Word was the Power. From that power shone the light of Divine Majesty. The Kingdom—along with the power of this world—was also attached to the Spirit <margin>p The Spirit.</margin> as its own property. This was generated out of the "Virgin of Wonders and Wisdom" from the Eternal Center of Nature, where Mary also stood with outward power, life, flesh, and blood. In this same way, Christ—the true Son of God and our Brother—gave his body to his disciples to eat and his blood to drink.

<margin>p Christ.</margin>

16. God is *a substance* within his heavenly Virgin (where heavenly physical reality <note>original: "Substantiality"</note> is perceived and takes form within the Tincture of Fire). God used the "Word" and "Heart" to take in the Tincture from Mary’s blood, where her soul lived. With the Word *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat" — Latin for "Let it be done," referring to God's creative command.</note> acting as the eternal, binding womb <note>original: "astringent Matrix"</note>, God gathered these elements and allowed them to become flesh and blood in a human way. 

Understand this: Eternal Substance, along with Wisdom (the *Eternal Virginity*), gave itself into the fallen <note>original: "perished"</note> Tincture and womb of Mary. The *Promised Word* was there, which also gave itself into that fallen life within the Eternal Substance. Thus, he became a *New Man* who was strange and unknown to the earthly man. In this way, this New Body of Christ—meaning *the Inward Christ* <margin>p Christ.</margin> who was covered by the mortal outward man—gave itself under the form of Bread and Wine (as an outward thing) into the Tincture of the Apostles' souls. Thus, Christ became a Man within the Apostles.

# Ch. 13. Of Christ’s Testaments.

Apostles in the *Tincture* <note>term: Tincture — a spiritual essence or transformative power that gives life and quality to matter.</note> of the soul; and that is the New Body which Christ has brought us from Heaven [of which he said: *No one goes to Heaven except the one who has come from Heaven*]. So, when we wholly yield ourselves up to him in obedience, and with our old will go out from ourselves into his will, and so enter into Christ’s Congregation and desire his flesh and blood with all his benefits, then he gives us this body and blood to eat and to drink. This is received by the Inward Man born of God, for the Body of Christ is <margin>The omnipresent and all-subsisting Body. <note>original: "Omnipræsens et Omnisubsistens Corpus"</note></margin> everywhere present in *Substance*: it contains the Second Principle [that is the *Angelic world*, according to which God is called Merciful and the *Eternal Good*].

17. For, to say that Christ feeds the soul with *Spirit without a Body* is not true. The Holy Spirit does not create a "Principle," but rather the Eternal Substantiality in which the Holy Spirit dwells. The Spirit proceeds from there in a form of many thousand innumerable essences; even that which has gone forth is the *Virgin of Purity*, namely, the Eternal Wisdom, in which all the wonders of this world were beheld from eternity.

18. Understand us correctly, according to its high and precious worth: *Adam* possessed that *Substantiality in which the Virgin of God consists*. The spirit of this world was given to him and breathed into him within that substance. But the essences were Paradisiacal and sprang up through the [one pure] Element which the Substantiality contains. However, the spirit of this world in *Adam* took that Substantiality into itself, into its own power [just as water takes the light (in a flaming red-hot iron) into itself and extinguishes it].

19. At first, the Heavenly Substantiality <note>term: Substantiality — in this context, the spiritual "matter" or essence of the heavenly realm.</note> held the power [or dominance]. But afterwards, when *Adam* turned back with his desire into the Earthly Substantiality, then the Earthly [Substantiality] gained the power and dominance. That is the cause by which *our ruined heavenly substance has become earthly. Therefore, God, with the heavenly substance within us, had to become Man*. In both the Heavenly *Virgin* and in the Earthly, God has become Man and has clothed our souls in the heavenly Substantiality again—namely, his heavenly body. Yet our earthly part must pass away, while the heavenly remains standing forever.

20. And yet, nevertheless, we are captivated poor sinners with the <margin>The Lord's Supper.</margin> *old Adam*, into which the Devil has an entrance. We often go out from the fair Image—understand that the soul often turns its will into the Outward Man. Therefore, God has appointed this Sacrament <note>original: "Testament"</note> so that when we turn again to him, he then gives our soul the New Garment again—namely, the New Body—and renews and feeds it.

21. He who once obtains the Body of Christ does not lose it, unless he spoils it as Adam did; it is only covered by the "old Adam" <note>term: Old Adam — the corrupt, fallen nature of humanity inherited from the first man.</note> and, moreover, passes into the Mystery. It is very possible for the soul to leave it; therefore, the soul should not be secure or careless, but watchful.

22. Therefore, know that Christ gave his disciples his true, omnipresent, eternal, divine body to eat, and his blood to drink, from which the Holy Spirit proceeds. The "inward mouth" which received it was the desiring will of their souls; for the soul of man has hungered and thirsted continually since the heavy fall after such flesh and blood, and puts it on as the garment of God. For the soul in itself is a *spirit* and has need of a *body*; and there it attains a body—a new, eternal, incorruptible body—within the old Adamic body.

23. Thus you are to know that the bread which Christ gave to his disciples was what the outward mouth took and gave to the belly. But the *word* of which Christ said, *“Eat, this is my body,”* that same word was the eternal body of Christ and had heavenly flesh and blood in it, and the soul received that as a new body. Thus, there were at once in the hand of Christ two kingdoms, namely, a heavenly and an earthly.

<margin>Note.</margin>
24. But you must know that the heavenly cannot be grasped or carried forth by the earthly. For the heavenly man—namely, the heavenly body of Christ *which was within the outward Christ*—filled the angelic world all at once and in eternity (that is, the second principle of God). Without that same bodily substance, God is not *known* at all, for the power of the Deity has manifested itself in it. Yet the outward image remains standing, so that in heaven people see the human nature palpably and perceptibly standing *in the form it was in here on earth*. You see nothing else in it but the majesty of the clarity of the brightness, which fills the angelic world. Wherever the majesty is now, there is the substantiality of Christ; for the Heart and the Word of God have *united it* in that substantiality. Just as we consider that the Word is *everywhere*, so is the substantiality (the body of the Word) everywhere, though indeed without an "image" <note>original: "Image" — here meaning a finite, localized shape like a physical body.</note>; for only the creature has the formation or image.

25. Behold, I give you an illustration: consider that all things are created out of water, and in water was all power and virtue; for you find that all things contain water, whether it is a stone, or flesh, or whatever it is. But "sulfur" <note>term: Sulphur — in Boehme’s alchemy-influenced theology, the active, formative energy or "soul" within matter.</note> is within it with the power of nature, which *forms* the substance.

26. Now behold: in the whole deep <note>term: Deep — the vast, infinite expanse of the created and uncreated universe.</note>, there is nothing but water, air, and fire, out of which the *substance*—namely, the body or the earth—came to be.

27. Now you can see quite clearly that the *Sun* (which is only one) causes this; it is also the power <note>original: "vertue"</note> and majesty within this physical <note>original: "Elementary"</note> substance. Everything belongs to the sun, and everything desires the sun, and the sun, with its power, provides the dominion [or government of everything in the universe].

28. Consider this through an analogy: God is the *Eternal Sun* in the second principle—meaning the heart, splendor, power, and majesty. The elements—fire, water, and earth—are (speaking analogically) [as it were] God the Father. Now the sun stands there as a body, as indeed it is, which resembles the creaturely *Christ*. The whole substance of the four elements resembles the *substantiality* <note>term: Substantiality — the spiritual "matter" or essence of the divine realm.</note> of the creature in which the sun's splendor shines. The *Sun* resembles the Word and the majesty, and the *four elements* resemble the power of the Body and the Father, out of whom the Son shines.

29. Therefore, know that in heaven, the Father's power is *everywhere, all over*, and the Word is within that power. The Word possesses the substantiality, which all belongs to the person of Christ; for Christ stands within the Father [as] *an image*, just as the sun stands within the elements.

30. If God were to reveal himself, the *whole world* would be *pure sun*, for the Deep <note>term: The Deep — the infinite, unmanifested space or "abyss" of the universe.</note> receives the sun's splendor. If there were no sun-like quality in the Deep, it *could not* receive the light; instead, it desires its own likeness. This is also how it is in heaven: the Son is everywhere in the Father and has become man. The total holy number three <note>term: Holy Number Three — the Trinity.</note>—without end or substance—has manifested itself as an image within substance, and that is *Christ*. We are his members; we are "gods" if we remain *in him*. He is our fountain and our light, and we are his stars. He gives us his body and power, and his splendor for [our] light.

<margin>† Or, Trinity.</margin>
31. In this way, he feeds us here on earth in *the [Lord's] Supper*. When we *desire it* with the power of his body and with the spirit which proceeds from that power (for that is the spirit and life of the power), then we receive the total holy † *Number Three*. This substantiality contains *sulfur* <note>term: Sulfur — in Boehme’s alchemical language, this represents the physical or substantial basis of a thing.</note>—meaning the body of Christ, which is the Father—and this *sulfur* possesses the power. Within the power is the light of life as another person; and from the power within the light, the scent and spirit of the power go forth. This spirit cannot be contained or held back by the power, yet it proceeds from the power and is the *Holy Spirit*.

## [ Concerning Baptism ].

<margin>Infant baptism. <note>original: "u Pædobaptisme."</note></margin>
33. And it is similar with the baptism of children. The soul consists of *two* things: *fire* and *water*. For the blood has *two* forms, namely *sulphur* and water. Sulphur gives the *tincture* <note>term: Tincture — in this context, a spiritual essence or "dye" that infuses matter with life and divine qualities.</note> and life, for it gives light, which is the burning out from the sulphur, and that is life. The *phur* is fire, and the *sul* is light. Out of the light comes *mildness*, which draws the *phur* back to itself and quenches its fierceness with it. This attraction makes the mildness *substantial*, which is *water*. *Mercury* <note>term: Mercury — representing the principle of movement, communication, and the "vital spirit" in alchemical theology.</note> creates the "Great Life" within it—that is, a life in the water—and the heavenly *Luna* <note>original: "Luna" — the moon, representing the feminine, cooling, and reflective principle that gives form to liquid.</note> nurtures it so that it turns into a liquid and into blood, in which is the *center of nature with its heavenly forms*.

34. Now observe: when the seed for the child is sown, then the tincture of the fire—namely the *man’s tincture*—is sown into the *tincture of Venus* <note>term: Venus — representing the water-life, desire, and the feminine principle of growth and attraction.</note>. Out of this proceeds a *twofold life*: a fire-life of the soul and, in Venus, a water-life of the spirit [or a water-spirit-life], which spring up together and become a man. And thus, both tinctures in *Adam* are now corrupted.

<margin>Of the great world <note>original: "x Macrocosmi."</note></margin>
35. They both would have remained captivated by the devil if the *Word of the Lord* <note>original: "Verbum Domini"</note>, which eventually became flesh, had not interposed in the middle as a mediator.

37. It is not that the *Holy Spirit* alone baptizes; indeed, he chiefly manages the *office* and takes the power of the *Trinity* <note>original: "Number Three"</note> with which he *baptizes*. And so when the *baptizer* says, "*I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit*," then the *Holy Spirit* takes hold in the *Trinity* and *baptizes* in the *water* of the *soul*, in the *water of life*, which is in the *blood* of the *tincture*, which contains the *spirit-life*—namely, the *second center of nature*. And so the *spirit* of the *soul* receives the power and *office* of the *Holy Spirit*; and here lies the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>.

38. *Dear brethren in Babel* <note>original: "Babell" — referring to the confusion of the worldly or false church</note>, do not just dance around on the outside of the *mystery*; enter in, or else you are not the *ministers of Christ*. You cannot *baptize* the *child*, but the *congregation of God* (which has the *faith*) *baptizes* it. A shepherd or a swineherd who simply believes that *baptism* is a *great hidden mystery* wherein the *Holy Trinity* baptizes, and that he himself is but the *servant*, *minister*, or *instrument* who performs only the outward work—he in his simplicity baptizes much better than you do.

You have a hard bit [to chew] of *Christ’s testaments*; if you will not go out from your *councils* into the *temple of Jesus Christ*, you must be completely cast away.

# Chapter 13: Of Christ’s Testaments.

40. [Pro]pagated yourselves, and not the office of Christ; but you have now become very few in Germany. Where there were a thousand of you, there are now scarcely a hundred. If you will not leave behind your human wit and your own inventions, God will so reject you that where there are now a hundred, there shall not remain ten of you, nor even a smaller number. Awake from your sleep, lest you go down into perdition into the abyss.

41. You say we laugh you to scorn: it may be you think so, for there is one who laughs you to scorn whom we know, and who shows it to us. He will suddenly awake; do not be so complacent and careless, but consider it. For no one takes anything for himself unless it is given to him by God, nor will this be spoken in vain.

<margin>Note.</margin>
42. O beloved and worthy Christendom, observe it well: do not say, "if our teachers do not lead us correctly, let them deal with it." O no, it concerns your very self; it will cost the loss of your body and soul. Dear Christendom has departed from all the apostolic <term>Apostolic: Relating to the original twelve apostles and their simple, spiritual teachings.</term> ordinances, virtue, and power, into human inventions and institutions. In stead of Christ's Kingdom, a pompous, stately, and hypocritical one has been set up through Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

<margin>Godly or pious.</margin>
43. Men set up ceremonies: O, if they had kept the true faith and had shown the people the divine way toward the new regeneration <note>original: "New Regeneration"; in this context, it refers to the spiritual rebirth of the soul through Christ.</note>, if they had shown them the clear countenance of God, then people would have departed from their sins into a divine life.

<margin>Or, husband.</margin>
44. But your wit and subtlety, O you whore <note>original: "whore"; a common 17th-century polemical term for a corrupt or "apostate" church, often referencing the 'Whore of Babylon' from the Book of Revelation.</note>, have blinded everyone. If my eyes had not been opened by God, how should I have known you? I would indeed have still worshipped you. The world shall seek you and at length find you; and then Europe shall be a crown, and Asia the husband, and Africa the country, and a simple shepherd shall lead us to pasture. If you understood this, you would look into yourself; but you will be blind until you are repaid. As you have poured out affliction, so you shall drink up misery and torment, for you have made it so very great as it is. You are a wild tree and shall be broken off. There is no remedy; your own wrath casts you to the ground, for you are weighed in a balance and are found too light, says the Spirit of the Great Wonders.

### The Magic out of the Wonders.
<note>original: "Magia"; in Boehme's philosophy, this refers to the divine "magic" or spiritual power that brings the internal will into external form.</note>

<margin>Or, the unit number.</margin>
45. A thing which grows out of a beginning has a beginning and an end, and grows no higher than the number from which it grows. But that which is in the One Number <note>original: "One Number"; the divine unity or the monad, which is eternal and indivisible.</note> is incorruptible, for it is only one and no more; there is nothing in it that can break it. For anything that is one is not at enmi- <meta>catchword: enmity</meta>

[is at] enmity with itself. But when there are two things in one, there is plain contrariety and strife. For that which is **one** does not strive against itself, but draws into itself and out of itself and remains **one**. Even if it seeks more within itself, it finds no more, and it can never be at odds with itself. For it is one thing; wherever it goes, it goes in one will. Where there are two wills, there is division or separation; for one will often goes inward and the other outward. If that thing has a body, then that kingdom or **government** in that body is at odds. If one enters into the other with enmity, that is a contrary will which goes against the other. Therein dwells the **Third Number**. This third number is a mixed essence derived from the first two and is against them both. It wants to be its **own** master, yet it also has **two wills** within itself from the first two: one of which tends toward the right hand and the other toward the left.

<margin>
e Or, Kingdom.
f Or, quash.
g Degree or pitch of its strength or limit.
h Foretells, divines, etc.
i Or, disturbance.
</margin>

46. Thus, the thing rises up from two into **many**, and every one has its own will. If this occurs in only one body, then it is at odds with itself because it has many wills and needs a judge to separate them and keep the wills in check. But if the wills are strong and will not be kept in check by the judge, but instead break out, then from one ^e^ **government** there become two. For that which has broken away judges or rules itself according to its own will and hates the first because it is not in its will. Thus, there is strife, with one desiring to ^f^ quash the other and so to elevate itself alone in one substance. If it cannot ^f^ quash the other (no matter how much opposition it makes), then each of them **increases** within itself to its highest ^g^ degree and is always in strife against the other. 

If it comes to pass that it has grown to its highest number—so that it can go no further—then it enters into itself and examines itself to see why it can grow no more. So it sees the **end** of the number and sets its will at the end of the number, desiring to break the **bond** or **limit** apart. In that will (which it directs at the end of the number to break it), the **prophet is born**. He is its own prophet and ^h^ foretells the errors in the will—how they cannot go further—and of the breaking of them. For he is born in the highest number of the crown, at the **end of the limit**, and speaks of the ^i^ disturbance <note>original: "Turba"; Jacob Boehme uses this Latin term to describe the spirit of turmoil or divine wrath that breaks down a system or "government" when it has reached its limit of corruption or complexity.</note> in its kingdom, how it shall end, and why it cannot go beyond its own number. Then he prophesies of a **new** [kingdom or government] which shall be generated again out of the breaking. # Chapter 13: Of Christ’s Testaments

...the pride of the kingdom [or government], and the covetousness and envy within it. Because that kingdom had only one root from which it grew, he now shows the evil twigs or branches that have grown out of that root. These branches represent the distraction and disturbance—or <term>Turba</term> <note>original: *Turba*; a Latin term used by the author to describe a spirit of turmoil, agitation, or a destructive force that disrupts divine order.</note>—of the kingdom, which destroys *the old tree* and drains its strength and sap until it must wither away.

47. He also shows the falsehood of these twigs and branches, which have stolen the tree's strength and thrown it to the ground. They claim to be a "new tree" and a "good kingdom" [or government]. They boast of this as if they were distinguished guests, showing great wit and a facade of devotion. Yet they have grown out of the old tree and are its own children, and thus they devour *their own father*. Therefore, the Prophet says they are not children but wolves; they have come to murder, devour, and establish themselves in place of the old tree. Their pride continues to drive them until they reach their limit, at which point they will be devoured by their own children in turn.

48. This is their own "prophet" which has grown upon their crown: for he declares the evil nature of the root from which the first tree grew. He shows the poison that infected the root, causing many conflicting wills to grow out of a single one, which is where strife and malice began.

49. And so, if the <term>Turba</term> has grown up within a thing, it turns unity into multiplicity. Where this multiplicity is at enmity with itself, the <term>Turba</term> also breaks that multiplicity apart. The original "will" for a thing desires only that one thing, which is its body and its delight. But multiplicity within a thing creates conflict; one will always wants to rise above the others, and the others will not tolerate it. From this comes envy and falsehood, which lead to anger and strife, where each part desires to break off and overthrow the other. Although the "first will" acts as a judge, the <term>Turba</term> has also sprouted in all the twigs and branches. This destroys obedience, so each will goes its own way and refuses to be judged or ruled. Instead, it takes authority for itself and despises *the Father* and all the other children (who are actually its own brothers and sisters). It claims that it alone is the tree and the source of its power, whereas it is actually only a broken, self-willed, proud murderer which *opposes itself against the first will—that is, the root.*

50. Now, when the Father sees his evil, disobedient child, he seeks a *remedy* to heal what is broken and pours oil into the wounds. But he finds that the oil acts as poison to them because they have turned their will away from the primary will—the root from which the healing oil flows—and the <term>Turba</term> has...

# Ch: 14. The Broad Way and the Narrow Way.

15. If you will not drive the Devil out of your heart, then he will not let you enter into God's will. If you keep the iniquity of falsehood in your heart, and so try to fight him using the merits and <term>satisfaction</term> <note>original: "satisfaction"; the theological concept of Christ paying the debt for human sin</note> of Christ, then you will be hindered; for the Devil strongly opposes it. He strives against the soul as long as he can; he does not let the soul go until it heaps all earthliness upon his neck and departs from it. When the soul does so, then it departs out of his territory, and then he is overcome. But oh, how he continually lays that [as a net] before it, and always goes about like a <term>fowler</term> <note>original: "Fowler"; a hunter of birds using nets or traps</note>, and if he possibly can, he will cast the earthly garment onto it again.

16. O, what a hard combat the poor soul must endure against the Devil! But in that struggle, the merits, satisfaction, and death of Christ are effective when the Devil has ensnared the poor soul again and will not let it go, but goes down with it into the abyss into *despair*. There the soul must take with it the sufferings and death of Christ, and walk with the Devil *through Hell into the death of Christ*, and out of Christ's death spring up with Christ into God again; then it is the **Lily** <note>In this context, the Lily represents the soul reborn in purity and divine light</note> which the Devil does not like to smell.

17. But for you to depend wholly on the *history* <note>original: "History"; meaning an intellectual or historical knowledge of the Bible without an inner spiritual transformation</note>, and to apply the merit, suffering, and death of Christ while still keeping the Devil lodging in your soul—that is a reproach to Christ. What does it benefit you to pray *that God would forgive you for Christ's sake* when you do not forgive all others? Your heart is full of revenge and robbery.

<margin>ⁿ Or, is fed by its own substance, which is its flesh and body.</margin>
18. You go to church, into the congregation of Christ, and you bring a false hypocrite, a liar, a covetous, angry, adulterous, proud person and soul *in with you*, and you bring that same person out with you again. What benefit have you gained? You go into the congregation to the *Supper of Christ* <note>The Lord's Supper or Holy Communion</note> and desire Christ's flesh and blood, and yet you keep the black Devil in you as a guest. What do you mean by this? You receive nothing but the severe anger of God. How will you feed upon Christ's flesh and blood if your soul is not inclined with all earnestness and sincerity toward God? Do you suppose that Christ's body and blood dwell in the earthly element in such a way that you can chew it with your teeth? No, friend, it is a more pure and subtle thing; the soul must grasp it; the mouth of the soul must receive it. But how shall it receive Christ if the Devil is still lodging in the soul? The soul must be in the will of God if it wishes to feed upon God; indeed, it can continually eat of Christ's flesh if it lives in the flesh of Christ; for every spirit <gloss>ⁿ</gloss> eats of its own body.

20. This is the right universal <note>original: "Catholike"; here meaning the universal, true Christian path rather than specifically the Roman Catholic Church</note> way of true faith. He who teaches and lives otherwise is *not appointed* as a shepherd by *Christ*, but is a shepherd who has sprung up of himself from his own <term>Art</term> <note>original: "Art"; referring to formal academic training, human skill, or "book learning" as opposed to divine inspiration</note> and reason. 21. Oh, you false bishops coming from the universities, how the Devil of pride has blinded you! You appoint shepherds over the lambs of Christ according to your own favor and respect. Saint *Paul* teaches you—just read it—what a heavy account you must give. Nothing matters to you but academic skill; but in the kingdom of Christ, such skill is but dross and dung. *God leads a pure heart by his own Spirit* if one turns toward him and submits to his will; to such a person, he teaches heavenly art.

25. O dear children, *open your eyes wide*. A Christian is not a wrathful soldier or warrior who desires the kingdom of this world; for Christ said, *My kingdom is not of this world*, otherwise my servants would *fight for it*. Saint Paul said, *Seek those things which are above, where Christ is*. We are called by Christ *out of this world* so that we might serve God with our souls and be in Christ, while being in this world with our bodies so that we may have maintenance and sustenance for them. Therefore, the *earthly life* ought to labor and maintain its body, but the *soul* should be lord and governor and rule the body. It should not allow the *starry spirit* <note>original: "Starry-Spirit"; refers to the influence of the physical cosmos or astrological forces on the human mind and lower nature</note> to practice any falsehood or fill itself with lies and deceit, for such things are brought into the soul.

Then you will surely *awake out of the sleep of the animal-like life* <note>original: "beastiall Life"</note> and consider what will follow hereafter when the spirit of the stars and elements leaves you. Think where your best jewel (which you yourself are) will then remain, and in what condition you will be *forever without end*. For we know that the soul dwells in the heart. 31. Observe this according to its precious depth: the **four forms** contain within them the **original of nature**. First, in the desiring will, the darkness enters into a desire along with the "attracting." So the desiring becomes strong, ¶ **harsh**, hard, and cold. This desiring creates an attraction and stirring within that strong harshness—these are the first two forms. The third form is the **great anguish**, arising because the desiring wants to be free; this stirs the anxious **wheel of nature** and, in the end, stirs up the **flash of fire**, which is the fourth form, as was mentioned at length before.

32. And so, that harsh attraction in the desiring of the will creates a great **covetousness** in the outward nature of this world. This causes the mind to want to attract everything to itself and possess it alone. Even if the mind cannot devour it, it still wants to own it and would not willingly give anything to anyone else. This is one root of the **abyss of Hell**, where the Devil vehemently assaults the soul so that it might not escape and come to the **light of God**.

40. For it is sufficiently known to us (seeing God is purely good) that he created nothing evil; for that which was not from eternity, was not in the creation.

<margin>e Quality, or living faculty.</margin>
41. God created no *Hell*, nor any *Devils*, but Angels: only Lucifer has turned himself away from meekness, and has flown out above the Cross of the Number Three <note>original: "Number Three"; a reference to the Trinity</note>, and has himself awakened the fire of anger in the flash <note>original: "flash"; in this context, the sudden ignition or manifestation of divine power or wrath</note>; which had remained *hidden in secret* from eternity; which is now his hell and habitation. 42. Therefore, dear children, since we know that we are thus surrounded with hell and the devils, in the anger of God, it is very necessary for us to fly *into humility*: and *therefore* Christ teaches us so very earnestly to study meekness, love, and mercy, that we should love one another, and should not so eagerly strive after the spirit of this world; for the devil slips into it and seduces us. We should watchfully take heed of pride, for the devil flies into it; and of *anger*, for that is the devil's sword, with which he commits all murders.

<margin>f Incarnate.</margin>
43. Oh, how lamentable a thing it is that the poor soul is *so* blinded that it does not know the heavy shackles and bonds in which it lies captive. The fire of hell rises up to its very lips; the *whole world* is full of snares which the devil has laid to catch the poor soul. If the eyes of the outward man should be opened, he would be terribly frightened; *Everything* that man touches or looks upon has a net and snare of the devil in it. This is because the soul enters into lust and into the dominion of this world. For if the soul completely surrenders itself to the lust, pleasure, and dominion of this world, then the Devil does not *sift* <margin>* Or, tempt.</margin> it so intensely. The Devil continually stirs it up, tickling the soul with these desires so that it might confidently and freely eat the forbidden fruit.

46. We find that human life is *threefold*, with three spirits together in *one*, as if they were but one spirit—and indeed, it is but one life. However, it has three "dominions" <note>original: "Dominions"; spheres of influence or ruling principles</note>, each of which has its own "Mother" <note>The source or origin of a specific nature</note> that provides or generates it. The "center of nature" with its forms (or properties) is the eternal life, for it is the "fire-life." The spirit that is generated and goes out from the center of nature, dwelling in the *tincture* <note>original: "Tincture"; a mystical term for the spiritual essence or 'dye' that gives life its quality</note>, is the eternal <margin>ʰ Life of the soul.</margin> ʰ life of the soul. Finally, the "air-spirit"—with the qualities or properties of the dominion of the stars—is the beginning, ending, and temporary life. This is the "beastly" life (the animal life which we have in common with animals).

47. Now, the soul is generated only from the *first two* spirits, and the *third* is breathed into it. This was not done so that the soul should enter into the third spirit and surrender to it (as Adam did), but so that the soul should mightily rule over it. Through this, the soul was meant to reveal the great wonders of God, which were seen from eternity in the Wisdom of God. For the *third* dominion is generated and created out of the *first*; and the *second* dominion was intended to stay in its own place (in the noble tincture) in Paradise, revealing the great wonders in the third. Therefore, man was made *Lord* over all things. He held the *tincture* (or life) of the earth in his own hand (or power), and *gold and silver* were as easy for him to find as any other visible thing. The tincture of the earth was his ornament and plaything, in a completely childlike way, without greed. He needed no other clothing; and just as gold was pure without dross, his childlike mind was also pure.

That which man should have ruled over now rules over him, and that is his *Fall*.

55. For we write what we ourselves have known and have seen with *spiritual eyes*. 56. When that springs up again, it produces *lilies without number*, and every spring, when the mind is renewed in *Christ*, it multiplies *tenfold*.

4. My dear children in Christ, and all you who have given yourselves up in *Christ* to the Kingdom of Heaven—you the chosen in *Christ*—this is how it is with our souls: our souls are stuck in such great restlessness. It is like a soldier in a battle who is constantly expecting death, where enemies press upon him from every side and strike at him, constantly desiring *his death*. Or it is like someone who has *fallen into a deep sea* and is swimming there, seeing no shore, and constantly *expecting* death as the water enters his mouth, who sighs and desires help from above. Or like someone falling into a *deep pit* where no help is seen, who also expects help from above.

5. So it is also with the poor soul: it has fallen into a dark *dungeon* and swims in dangerous, deep water, where it is surrounded by enemies on every side who all strike at it. Everyone wants to murder it, and it *sees no help around it*. If it searches through its body—through its flesh and blood, and even through its marrow and bones—it finds they *all* are its enemies, which lead it toward the *Abyss* <note>original: "Abysse"; in Böhme’s work, this often refers to the dark, chaotic "groundless" state outside of God's light.</note>.

6. The *spirit of this world* (operating in flesh and blood) draws the soul down and bows it to the ground, into the depths of the waters, and continually desires to drown it; for it only wants to maintain and pamper the bestial <note>original: "Beastiall"; referring to the animalistic, earthly nature of human life as opposed to the spiritual.</note> life.

<margin>d The Eternal Nature.</margin>
7. So also *the Devil* draws it mightily down into the Abyss and would gladly throw it into the eternal, aching source [or torment] of hell. If the soul resists, he strikes at it with the anguish of hell so that it should despair and throw itself into the Abyss. There, the soul has no helper with it or around it, nor can it see any help appearing, until it raises itself upward into the love and mercy of God. There, it must leave and *forsake* everything that is in its "house" <note>referring to the soul's worldly attachments and its identification with the physical body</note> and must wind its way completely through it like a spirit without substance. That is, it must go out with its will from all its thoughts and out from its entire mind into the *mercy of God*, into the first original <gloss>d</gloss> Mother, where it was *only a seed* before the creation of the world.

<margin>e Or, received.</margin>
8. And when it arrives there, it finds that the same Word which created it has become man. The soul casts itself into this Word and eats of that humanity as a pure and new body, in which there is no source [or quality] of enmity, but only a meek, pure, and longing love. There, its will is <gloss>e</gloss> accepted by God, and the Holy Spirit enters into its will and brings heavenly refreshment and comfort to the poor captive soul. In this way, it feeds on the flesh of the Eternal Word—of its original Mother—and drinks of the water of eternal life, *in which*, before the world began, it was only a seed.

<summary>Böhme uses metaphors of drowning and warfare to describe the soul's entrapment in the material world and its struggle against the devil. He explains that salvation is found by turning the will away from worldly thoughts and returning to God's mercy through the humanity of Christ.</summary>

## Ch: 16. Of Praying and Fasting.

<margin>Of God's Love.</margin>

Briefly, the whole Scripture is full of such examples.

<margin>Awakened from death.</margin>

Then he sighed to his Father and awakened the "Center of Nature" and the Word in the center of nature on the "Cross of the Number Three" <note>This is a reference to Böhme’s mystical geometry, where the "Number Three" represents the Trinity and the "Cross" is the point of divine manifestation.</note>. # Of Praying and Fasting. Ch. 16.

...sounds forth outwards and raises up the Body of the Essences <note>original: "Body of the Essences" — in this context, refers to the spiritual substance or inner nature that constitutes the soul's true form.</note>. For the souls of men are all, as it were, *one soul*, for they are all propagated out of one single soul. Therefore, they will all hear the voice of the human soul in Christ and arise with their bodies.

14. So then, when we pray to God, God hears our soul in the Center <note>original: "Centre" — in the author's mystical philosophy, this is the innermost point of origin within the soul where spiritual forces meet.</note> *within ourselves*. That is, the soul presses forth with its repenting will out of the Center of Anguish, out of the Abyss of Hell, and also out of the spirit of this world, into the second Principle—into God—which is also in the soul. For all *three* Principles are in the soul: namely, the two eternal ones <note>The eternal principles of Light/Heaven and Darkness/Wrath.</note> and the corruptible one, which brings the death of this world.

<margin>*Or, manifests, or reveals.*</margin>
15. Understand us accurately according to its high worth, in this way: God the Father does not move himself [when you pray]; *the Holy Spirit* alone moves himself. Though that indeed does not benefit us either; but the Word which has created our soul has become man, and that Word has the Holy Spirit in it. He goes forth from the Father in the Word and meets the calling mind and will, and *opens* himself from *within* outwards into the soul. For the outward beastial <note>original: "Beastiall" — referring to the animalistic, physical body that is driven by earthly instincts rather than spirit.</note> body *is not worthy* of the Holy Spirit, that he should open himself in it. Though it sometimes happened to the Saints that he went forth from the soul into the outward Principle; and then the body *triumphs* and, for very joy, does not know what has happened to it. But in the new body of the soul in Christ—when the soul attains the body of Christ—the Holy Spirit dwells *in that*.

16. And so when the Devil comes and tries to set upon the soul from beneath, in the first Principle <note>The "first Principle" represents the harsh, fiery, and dark foundation of existence where the Devil operates.</note>, in the center of the first four forms to the source of the fire, then the will of the soul presses into the flesh of Christ, into the second Principle—inwards into itself. There it is refreshed and released, and the Devil must go down; for that life does not suit his taste. Yet he is so furious that he sets upon the soul as often as he perceives it to be *secure and careless*, or whenever it burdens itself even a little with falsehood and wickedness. He *always seeks* an opportunity where he might find his nest open for him.

17. Therefore, dear children: when you pray, do not think that God dwells far away from you, and so neither hears you nor sees you; that is a false concept and opinion. Indeed, those who *will not* enter into God—those who stick fast in their malice and iniquity and retain wickedness in their soul—*those* indeed *are not heard*. He who cries to God that he would outwardly accept his words, yet retains the Evil One in his soul, *he mocks God*. God does not dwell outwardly; for the outward is the beastial...

# Of Praying and Fasting. Ch. 16.

...beastial starry spirit <note>The "starry spirit" refers to the sidereal or astral body—the part of human nature influenced by the physical stars and elements, distinct from the eternal soul.</note>: he dwells inwardly in himself. The outward substance is only a figure and likeness of God. Indeed, it is of God and generated out of the inward center, and expressed <insert>[or spoken forth]</insert> through the *Verbum Fiat* <note>original: "Verbum Fiat" — Latin for "The Word: Let it be done," referring to God's creative command in Genesis.</note>; but it is *not* the substance of the Trinity <note>original: "Number Three"</note>, which is a substance and Spirit in the Trinity, above nature. Yet it dwells in nature within itself, incomprehensible to nature, just as the wind and the light are not contained by the fire, and yet are the spirit, brightness, and life of the fire.

18. Therefore, when you wish to *pray*, put away the abominations from your soul and enter into yourself. That is, you must loathe those abominations and form a will and purpose in your soul that you will *not* let such abominations into you anymore. Also, you must not *allow* your will to get stuck in any <gloss>1</gloss> abomination and despair; for when you despair, you sink yourself down into the Abyss <note>original: "Abysse" — in this context, the chaotic void or the state of total separation from God's light.</note>.
<margin>1 Lusts and unchastity.</margin>

19. But consider that it is the *dear will and pleasure of God* that you press earnestly and strongly through, and leave the abominations to the Devil to hang around his own neck. You have vainly rioted and spent your beauty and righteousness with the Devil and with the *Antichristian Whore* <note>original: "Antichristian Whore" — a common Reformation-era term for spiritual corruption or a false church system, often identified with the "Whore of Babylon."</note>; you are among the swine at *Babel* <note>original: "Babell" — meaning Babylon, symbolizing a state of spiritual confusion, worldliness, and captivity.</note>. Having lost your goods, you eat grains and husks with the swine; you are naked and torn, and are not worthy to be called His son. Consider and imagine this within yourself, for it is true; and so come with true conversion out of the filth and mire of the swine to our Ancient Loving Father, and *pray for His grace and favor*, that He would make you even just one of His hired servants in His court. Acknowledge to Him your evil deeds, and that you are not worthy to be called His son. Behold, dear soul, *observe this: it is the very precious truth*.

20. When you enter into yourself in this way and search out your abominations and the husks of the Devil and of the world, which you have devoured for so long, and consider God and His mercy, then *do not turn back again to the hogsty*. Do not say, "I am ashamed to come before my good old Father; I dare not come into His sight because of my great shame and abomination, for I was a glorious son and now am a naked swineherd." Instead, consider that your Father cares more about you, His lost prodigal son, than you do about His favor and love, which you have willfully thrown away.

21. Simply form a loving, humble, submissive, and obedient will and purpose, and *come*. Come away from the swine; leave the husks to the world. Let the swine devour them and feed themselves fat, but you must enter into yourself and knock at your evil heart;

The *new son* pleases him better than the one who had stayed in the house. That elder son thought that he alone was the heir, and that the Kingdom of Heaven belonged to him; he believed he had earned it and had not left the house; he thought the keys of the treasure belonged to him, and the other was but a swineherd. All this does not divert the Father; instead, he is merry with his servants, the angels and holy souls. # Of Praying and Fasting. Ch: 16.

<margin>ᵒ So that the contentions, brawling, and disputes may cease.</margin>

27. When Christ drove the devil out of the lunatic who was possessed, his disciples said to him: *Master, why could we not drive him out?* Then Christ said: *This kind does not go out except by fasting and prayer.*

<margin>ᵖ Or, Highest Age.</margin>

He now sends you *many* messengers and calls you in their voice, and he will send more to you. Why do you despise them and kill them? *Test them* to see whether their spirit is born of God or not, or whether they seek their own way for the sake of their bellies in the Antichrist. Surely it is time to wake from sleep; no joking matter will follow. You should not dare to joke so with the *Keys of the Holy Spirit* <note>original: "Keyes of the Holy Ghost"; a reference to the "Keys of the Kingdom" or authority to forgive sins</note> and make conclusions about faith according to your own opinions, tenets, and conceits. *Faith* will not be birthed by legal conclusions and church canons; rather, it is awakened by true sincerity, by being obedient children of Christ.

# Of Praying and Fasting. Chapter 16

29. Saint Paul did not say to his disciple: "Argue about the mysteries of God." Instead, he said, "Awaken or stir up the *gifts* that are in you." No man’s own cleverness can do this, much less the pride of the universities <note>original: "High Schools"</note>, which they cloak with hypocrisy and hide under the mantle of the *Holy Spirit*. Why do you draw conclusions about the *body* and the *person* of Christ? Do you have the power and authority to do so? Is it not a *mystery* to you? You understand nothing of it unless you are born again in *Christ*. Does he not say, "Behold, I am with you even to the end of the world"? If he is with you, why then do you seat yourselves upon his throne and deny his presence? Are you not like *Pilate*, who sentenced *Christ*? From whom do you receive the might and authority to establish doctrines and *Articles of Faith*? Are you *his* masters? If so, you are not children. Take care that you do not prove to be the older son in the house, who fights over the inheritance, power, and *authority*, and yet continues to be a proud, angry grumbler against the Father. Dear children, it is useless to go that way. Christ said to his disciples, when he drove the devil out of the possessed man (the "lunatic")—which the disciples could not do by their own reason—*This kind does not go out except by fasting and prayer.*

<margin>¶ A purse-net <note>A bag-shaped net used for catching game or fish; here used as a metaphor for a trap.</note></margin>
30. Dear brothers, you will not be able to drive the devil out of *us* if you do not have Christ with you. Your academic skill and logical conclusions will do nothing but cause people to turn away from God into their own self-will. We must fast and pray so that we do not fall into temptation and into the nets and snares of the devil within our own reason. For the devil always holds his net in front of reason, and whoever falls into it imagines he is caught in *Christ’s* fishing net; but he is actually taken in Antichrist's ¶ net. Reason understands nothing of the kingdom of God except for the outer husk; its virtue and power remain hidden to reason unless it is born in God. Only then does reason go forth like a burning fire *in the Spirit* of God, but the Spirit does not let it fly too high; rather, the Spirit bows it to the earth in humility, 
<margin>* Satan</margin>
for he knows the † *Warrior* <note>Referring to the divine power or Christ within the believer.</note> who fights against [corrupt] reason.

31. A watchful life is required—one that is disciplined and not overwhelmed by the fleshly, *indulgent* spirit of this world. It should not be a life that is always drunken and full. For as soon as the soul is inflamed with the vigor and power of the earthly spirit, God’s Spirit withdraws into its own realm <note>original: "Principle"</note>. Then the soul is captivated by the spirit of this world, and the devil gains access to it. At that point, its former wisdom and understanding (which it knew in God) is changed into mere outward reason—and yet, the person still wrongly supposes that it is *God’s Spirit* leading them.

Every member has its own office or work in revealing the wonders of God. We do not all bring the same words, but we share one spirit in Christ. Each person has his own gift imparted to him to reveal in God, so that the great mysteries of God may be made manifest, and the wonders foreseen from eternity in His wisdom might be revealed—which is the purpose for which the soul was created by God.

The soul is permitted to be *zealous*, but it does *better* to live in meekness, through which it enters into the Majesty of God and is a totally beloved child. What does it benefit me to pour out fire upon my brother and burn myself in it? It is more blessed to continue under the Cross in patience and in meekness than to bring down fire from Heaven <note>An allusion to Luke 9:54-55, where the disciples were rebuked for wanting to call down fire on those who rejected Jesus</note>.

37. *Christ* has come to seek and to save that which was *lost*, not to awaken his anger against us, but so that he might help us out of the jaws of the Devil. He has regenerated us in himself to be a living creature in God and has brought us quite through the fire of his Father’s anger. He has broken the chains so that we might follow him in love and meekness, as children should follow their parents. Therefore, he faithfully teaches us what we should do and how we should pray.

## Of the Lord's Prayer

<margin>
z Guidance.
a Circumscribed or limited in its interpretation.
b Guidance.
</margin>
38. The *Prayer* which he has taught us is an instruction and teaching of all whatever we should do and leave undone, and what we should ask and expect from God. It is always to be understood according to the *Three Principles* <note>Boehme’s cosmological system involving the dark world (fire/anger), the light world (love/grace), and the physical world</note>, to which we will here provide a short z introduction <note>original: "Manuduction"; a guiding or leading by the hand</note>. However, this explanation cannot be a limited or concluded, for the Spirit in the prayer encompasses all of *Eternity*, as well as Nature and everything; so that no tongue can sufficiently explain it. The more it is considered, the more is found in it. Yet we will venture upon it and give the reader a b guidance—not to tie or limit the Spirit, for the Spirit rises up in everyone’s soul as virtue and power are given from the wonders of God. And it is the same with the Gospel: it is not tied to any single exposition. The more any search into it, the more they find therein. For the Spirit of God itself teaches us to pray.

# Chapter 16: On Praying and Fasting.

Praying correctly also presents us to God. For we do not know what we should say; our entire effort of praying and conversion consists only in the will and purpose—that we give ourselves up to God. God the *Holy Spirit* himself brings about the springing up and growing through himself in God. He drives forth the blossom of the soul's new body from the *Divine Center* out through the soul, so that the fruit of eternal life springs forth from the *soul's body* with many branches and beautiful fruit. It stands as a *glorious tree* in the *Kingdom of God*. So, when we pray, our soul eats of many heavenly fruits, all of which have grown out of the body of the soul as if from a *heavenly soil* or ground. The soul eats of them again in prayer, and they are its food at the *Table of God*. Thus it eats *from the word of the Lord* <note>original: "ex verbo Domini"</note> concerning which Christ says: *Man lives not by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.*

<margin>
c The Our Father <note>original: "Pater Noster"</note>.
</margin>
39. c The Lord's Prayer provides a very deep and excellent understanding in the *Language of Nature* <note>Boehme's term for a mystical, universal language where the sound of words reveals the essence of things</note>. It expresses the *eternal birth*, all *three principles*, and the *lamentable fall of man*, while showing him his *regeneration in Christ*. It shows him what he should do and how he should behave so that he may return to the *divine union*, and it shows how kindly the Spirit of God meets him.

<margin>
d Understanding and meaning.
e This likely refers to his treatise called *The Holy Weeks*, or the *Prayer Book*, which was not finished.
</margin>

### [ The Entrance ]

->*Our Father in Heaven.*<- <note>original: "Unser vatter im Himmel"</note>
->**Our Father [who is] in Heaven.**<-

41. When we say: *Our Father in Heaven* <note>original: "Unser vatter im Himmel"</note>, the soul raises itself up into all **Three Principles** <note>Boehme’s term for the three realms of existence: the dark-fire world, the light-fire world, and the external world</note> and gives itself up to that source from which it was created. We understand this very exactly and accurately through the **Language of Nature** <note>the idea that the sounds of words reveal the true essence of the things they name</note>. For the syllable *un-* represents God's eternal will toward nature; the syllable *-ser* includes the first four forms of nature, which constitute the **First Principle** <note>the "dark" foundation or source of energy in Boehme’s system</note>.

42. *Vatter* <note>original: "Vatter"; German for "Father"</note> provides the two distinctions between the two principles. The syllable *va-* is the **Matrix** <note>original: "Matrix"; meaning the womb or generative source</note> upon the **Cross**, and the syllable *-tter* is **Mercury** <note>in Boehme’s alchemy, the active, moving spirit or "wheel" of nature</note> in the center of nature. These are the two "mothers" within the eternal will from which all things have come to be. One separates itself into fire, and the other into the light of gentleness and into water. This is because *va-* is the mother of the light, which provides **Substantiality** <note>physical or spiritual substance</note>, and *-tter* is the mother of the fire's **Tincture** <note>the spiritual essence or life-force</note>, which provides the great and strong life. The word *Vatter* represents both of them together.

43. When we say *im* <note>German for "in"</note>, we understand the innermost part—namely, the heart—from which the spirit goes out. The syllable *im* proceeds from the heart and sounds through the lips, and the lips keep the heart unawakened in its innermost place.

44. When we say *Him-*, we understand the creation of the soul. The syllable *-mel* <note>together forming "Himmel," German for "Heaven"</note> is the angelic soul itself, which the heart has grasped on the cross in the center between the two "mothers." With the word *Him-*, it framed the soul into a creature—namely, into *mel*. Because *Him-* is the dwelling place of *mel*, the soul is created in Heaven—that is, in the loving matrix or mother.

### The First Petition.

->*Your name be hallowed.*<- <note>original: "Dein Nahme werde geheiliget"</note>
<margin>h Or, sanctified.</margin>
->**May your name be ^h^hallowed.**<-

45. When we say *Dein* <note>German for "your"</note>, we understand how the poor soul swims in the water of this world and how it throws itself with its will into the principle of God. With the syllable *Dein*, it enters into the voice of God.

46. In the syllable *Nah-*, the soul leans inward, and in the syllable *-me* <note>together forming "Nahme," German for "Name"</note>, it grasps heavenly substance. This is all accomplished through the will of the soul.

Then *-hei-* <note>OCR reads "-bei-", likely a transcription error for "-hei-" in *ge-hei-li-get*</note> is the powerful entry upon the **Cross**, into the **Number-Three** <note>the Trinity</note>, where the soul's will presses into the Majesty, into the Light of God.
